t: MV_HEADLESS_PROFILE names a private host-owned JSON profile; when config_template.runtime_admitted is false requests return UNAVAILABLE before process creation. MV_HEADLESS_ONLY=1 bootstraps without graphical/SRF paths, needs the core registration variables and XDG_RUNTIME_DIR, and creates no capsule, frame, view or recording manager.
The headless service is bounded by MemoryMax=512M, MemorySwapMax=0, CPUQuota=100%, TasksMax=64 and RuntimeMaxSec=180 [TARGET], with no restart and requests never retried.

README states hello is capped at 5 seconds and idle reads at 30 seconds [CITED: contracts/v0.2/README.md transport table], with missing values refusing startup; the env runtime sets exactly these values.

README documents that MV_SRF_STATE_DIR must be a current-uid 0700 directory appended as --state-dir to srf-identity-surface, a missing final directory is created privately, the variable is stripped from the child environment, and SRF_IDENTITY_STORE_ROOT and SRF_PROXY_REGISTRY pass through.

Process entry of mv-daemon-adapter: locks the main goroutine to its OS thread (so the Linux parent-death signal stays bound), installs a SIGINT/SIGTERM-cancelled context, binds parent lifetime, builds the Runtime from environment with daemon.RuntimeFromEnv and then calls daemon.Run with os.Args[1:]. Any configuration error is printed to stderr and the process exits 2; otherwise the exit code is Run's.

prctl(PR_SET_PDEATHSIG, SIGTERM) makes the adapter receive SIGTERM when the launching app dies. If prctl fails the errno is printed; if the parent PID changed before the binding took effect it prints "launching parent exited before lifetime binding". Both exit with status 2 before any configuration is read.

Crate guest-command-broker 0.2.5, edition 2021, rust-version 1.97, its own empty [workspace]; exact-pinned deps libc =0.2.191, serde =1.0.229, serde_json =1.0.154, sha2 =0.10.9. Release profile keeps overflow-checks = true and panic = "abort", so an arithmetic overflow aborts PID1 instead of wrapping.
Package manifest for the standalone guest broker crate; it declares its own empty workspace so it builds apart from the parent daemon-adapter tree.

Feature rewind-profile gates the second binary rewind-command-broker (src/bin/rewind-command-broker.rs, required-features = ["rewind-profile"]) and the rewind module; the default build produces only the normal broker.

Standalone Cargo project for the ARM guest command broker: it implements the MVGC transport and a single-threaded guest PID1 command dispatcher. It is a source candidate, not a runtime acceptance, and must never be launched as a host command.

README states the transport limits [CITED: daemon-adapter/guest-command-broker/README.md]: send queue 128 KiB, a blocked frame fails after at most 3000 ms capped by guest lifetime, no retry or reconnect, output counters advance only when a full frame is written, and stdout+stderr combine to at most 65536 retained bytes per job; overflow terminates the job and can never become normal completion.

Guest lifetime is 60000 ms from startup and is never extended; job deadlines reserve 1000 ms for closure; the host's shorter 55000 ms lifetime is external [CITED: daemon-adapter/guest-command-broker/README.md]. Any socket/exec/cgroup/cleanup uncertainty powers off the guest and must stay unknown at the host; no fabricated job result is emitted.

Validation boundary: pure tests and a static ARM64 build cover framing, schema bounds, identity, history and status decoding only; they do not prove mount behavior, cgroup enforcement, vsock/BusyBox/seccomp compatibility, real cancellation or native closure. Host tests must have no host installs, network, shell-command probes or guest effects.
Fixed guest-only boot layout: cmdline binding, proc/sysfs/cgroup2 mounts, jail construction and poweroff; called from main and the rewind binary, never from host tests.
Fixed job identity JOB_UID = 10000 and JOB_GID = 10000, and guest lifetime GUEST_MS = 60000 ms measured on CLOCK_MONOTONIC from startup.

Kernel cmdline must be at most 8192 bytes without NUL (else "cmdline bound") and contain exactly one token mv_guest_command=1 and exactly one mv_nonce= of 64 lowercase hex characters (else "guest boot binding"); uppercase hex, a duplicate marker or a second nonce are refused.

Every bootstrap mount re-checks authority; a failing mount prints "guest_broker mount_failed target=<path> errno=<n>" and a failing mkdir prints "guest_broker mkdir_failed target=<path> errno=<n>" before the error reaches main (phase=prepare or read_boot) and the guest powers off.

The only effect before the boot marker is checked: verify /proc is a root-owned non-writable directory, mount proc with nosuid,nodev,noexec and hidepid=2, confirm PROC_SUPER_MAGIC, read at most 8193 bytes of /proc/cmdline and pass them to Boot::parse.
With feature rewind-profile, read_rewind_boot repeats the same proc mount and 8193-byte cmdline read but hands the text to rewind::Boot::parse; the normal Boot and lifetime are unchanged.

prepare() order: remove validated /dev/console, umask 077 and ignore SIGPIPE, mount sysfs and cgroup2, bind the empty /etc/empty-cmdline read-only over /proc/cmdline, create tmpfs /sandbox (size=2m), bind /bin, /etc, /dev, /proc read-only inside it, mask /sandbox/proc/cmdline separately, mount /sandbox/work tmpfs size=64m mode 0700 uid/gid 10000 with /sandbox/work/tmp, then remount /sandbox read-only.

prepare() refusals: "console node custody" when /dev/console is not root:root char 5:1 mode 0600 nlink 1, and "empty cmdline source" when /etc/empty-cmdline is not a zero-length regular file without group/other write; either ends in poweroff at phase=prepare.
Console unlink is allowed only for uid 0, gid 0, S_IFCHR, mode exactly 0600, device major 5 minor 1 and nlink 1, keeping the console outside the job's /dev bind.
poweroff() calls reboot(RB_POWER_OFF) after an authority check; it is the single terminal effect for every guest outcome.
Single-threaded guest actor that runs host exec/cancel/stop requests one at a time; every effect requires the GuestAuthority guard.

History: at most 256 distinct request_ids and 64 distinct job_ids per session; a reused request id refuses "request reused or history exhausted", a reused job id, a 65th job or any exec after Stop refuses "job reused/stopped/exhausted".
The first terminate cause wins (cancel, stop, timeout or output_limit); it sends SIGTERM to the process group and schedules cgroup.kill 250 ms later.
If the child writes anything to its exec-error pipe (pre-exec setup or execve failed) the broker refuses "child pre-exec failed", which is fatal and powers off; EOF on that pipe marks exec_ok.

Retained output is sent as output events of at most 16384 bytes per chunk with per-stream chunk_index counters starting at 0; each enqueue carries (stream, length) so sent counters advance on full write.

history.request() and history.job() return Err with the ? operator, not an error frame, so a duplicate request_id, a reused job_id or history exhaustion ends serve() and powers the guest off; the host sees no reply, only connection loss.

exec is answered with error code BUSY when a job is active, Stop has been accepted, or the send queue is not idle; it is answered INVALID when the relative cwd does not resolve inside the jail workspace.

exec admission: split payload into command and stdin at command_bytes, Deadline = min(now + timeout_ms, lifetime end - 1000 ms), create job cgroup with Limits 128 MiB memory, 64 pids, guest 256 MiB, reset sent counters, fork the blocked child, attach it to the cgroup, release it, then queue accepted{op:exec}. Any failure in these steps is fatal (poweroff), not a reply.

cancel is answered INVALID when there is no active job, run_request_id or job_id does not match, a cancel was already accepted, the terminal frame is queued, or the leader was already reaped; otherwise accepted{op:cancel} is queued before SIGTERM is sent.

stop is answered INVALID when already stopping; otherwise accepted{op:stop, job_id:null} is queued, all future exec is fenced, and the active job (if its terminal is not yet queued) is terminated with cause stop. Any other kind after HELLO refuses "unexpected actor frame".

Each loop step: poll exec pipe, feed stdin, drain stdout/stderr, queue output, terminate on overflow (output_limit) or deadline (timeout), reap, cgroup.kill after leader exit or at kill_at. job_finished is queued only when leader status is known, no children remain, cgroup populated=0, both pipes at EOF and the send queue is idle.
Closure refusals, all fatal: "missing exec closure", "output overflow after different terminal cause", and "unsent output" when sent counters differ from retained stdout/stderr lengths.

A normal exit racing an accepted cancel or stop reports cause exit with the exit code while the control id stays in the frame; a signal death reports the requested cause (or exit); a stopped/non-terminal status refuses "nonterminal wait status".

On any serve error the active job gets SIGTERM and cgroup.kill, then the broker reaps for at most 1000 ms (capped at lifetime end) before returning to main, which powers off; no job_finished is emitted.

serve(): verify jail, prepare cgroups, accept the vsock peer, then loop flush -> retire finished job -> step job -> on stopping with no job and empty queue send stopping and return -> receive. The first frame must be hello ("HELLO required") and triggers ready; reaching the lifetime end refuses "guest lifetime expired".
One thread services transport, job pipes and reaping in a polling loop; Transport::wait polls the socket for 10 ms, and fork_blocked separately insists the process has exactly one task.

Rewind-only cleanup after disconnect or error: requires child reaped, no children, job cgroup empty, both pipe EOFs and the terminal-jobs tree quiescent within 1000 ms, else "rewind cleanup unknown" (or "cleanup clock" on clock overflow); any error is fatal.

Rewind session: refuses "rewind admission not quiescent" if cgroups or children remain; uses cgroup names rw_<epoch>_<n>; the first frame must equal the reset-derived HELLO exactly; an error whose text is "connection EOF" returns Disconnected so a new reset can be accepted, Stop returns Stopped; the lifetime end passed is u64::MAX - 10000, so only the 60000 ms timeout_ms cap bounds jobs.

GuestAuthority has only a private field, so code outside guard.rs cannot construct it; every effectful function in the crate takes &GuestAuthority, which means no effect is reachable without a successful detect().
Capability token proving a fresh observation of root PID1 on aarch64; required by every effectful call in bootstrap, sandbox, spawn, supervision, transport, dispatch and rewind.
Admission requires pid == 1, euid == 0 and uname machine == "aarch64"; otherwise refusal "root PID1 on aarch64 is required".
check() re-runs the uname/getpid/geteuid observation on every call, so each mount, fork, socket or cgroup write re-verifies root PID1 on aarch64 rather than trusting a cached result.

Library root exporting guard, output, sandbox, seccomp, spawn, supervision, bootstrap, dispatch, transport and wire (rewind only with feature rewind-profile). Every refusal in the crate is built by refused(), an io::Error of kind PermissionDenied whose message is the refusal string; main prints it as detail=<string> before poweroff.

Normal guest PID1 entry: GuestAuthority::detect, then phases clock -> read_boot -> prepare -> serve (dispatch::serve with lifetime end start + GUEST_MS). Whatever the outcome, including a clean Stop, it calls bootstrap::poweroff and exits 78; there is no reconnect or restart path.
Binary guest-command-broker: the normal PID1 program run inside the ARM64 guest image; called by the guest kernel as init, never by host code.
When not root PID1 on aarch64 the binary prints "guest broker requires root ARM64 PID1" and exits 78 without any mount or poweroff; this is what a host-side accidental launch shows.

Any startup or session error is logged on the guest console as "guest_broker failed phase=<clock|read_boot|prepare|serve> errno=<raw_os_error> kind=<ErrorKind> detail=<refusal string>" and the guest powers off; phase markers "guest_broker phase=read_boot|prepare|serve" precede each phase, so the last printed phase locates the failure.
Combined bounded stdout/stderr store for one job; dispatch::Job owns one and spawn::drain fills it.
Output buffer requires an explicit combined bound 1..=65536 bytes; 0 or more than 65536 refuses "explicit combined output bound required". dispatch always uses 65536.

push() stores bytes only while stdout+stderr combined is below the limit, keeps streams in separate vectors, and sets exceeded when any byte is dropped; success_admissible() is false once exceeded, which forces cause output_limit downstream.

Opt-in disposable REWIND guest (ARM64 only, feature rewind-profile), never used by the normal broker; the host authority must revoke old epochs across RAM rollback because guest RAM cannot prove freshness alone.
Reset framing constants: MAGIC "RWR1", MAX_RESET 4096 bytes, RESET_MS 3000 ms, MAX_SAFE 9007199254740991.

Rewind cmdline must be at most 8192 bytes without NUL, must not contain any mv_guest_command= token, and needs exactly one mv_rewind=1 and one 64-lowercase-hex mv_nonce; otherwise "rewind boot binding".

Reset JSON (1..=4096 bytes, "reset size") is closed with deny_unknown_fields ("closed reset JSON"): schema "rewind_guest_reset/v0.2", op "reseed", 64-hex boot_token and challenge, 128-hex entropy not all zeros, session_id 1..=128 chars [A-Za-z0-9._:-], epoch and command_generation 1..=MAX_SAFE ("reset fields"); identities are checked through the MVGC hello validator.

Each reset must carry the boot nonce, a strictly greater authority_epoch and command_generation, and an unseen session_id, challenge and SHA-256 of entropy, with at most 1024 sessions; otherwise "reset authority/replay fence".
After a reset, the first MVGC frame must be a hello whose canonical metadata equals the reset-derived hello with the fresh guest nonce; otherwise "reset/HELLO identity mismatch".
Counter advances in whole seconds from the monotonic clock and is logged as "rewind_counter value=<n>"; refusals "counter clock reversed", "counter exhausted", "counter clock overflow".

Rewind framing: peer must be CID 2 ("rewind host CID"); header is RWR1 plus big-endian u32 length 1..=4096 ("reset magic/header", "reset size"); the reset must arrive within 3000 ms ("reset deadline", "reset EOF"); the reply must fit 4096 bytes and send within 3000 ms ("reply size", "reply deadline", "reply send zero").

A root-only /.rewind-random char device 1:8 is created, opened, checked ("random device custody") and unlinked; reseed decodes 64 entropy bytes ("entropy encoding"), adds them with ioctl R,3 and reseeds with ioctl R,7, then reads a fresh 32-byte guest nonce via getrandom ("random read zero").

Rewind loop: require quiescent cgroups and no children ("rewind fence not empty"), log "rewind_fenced counter=<n>", accept, read and validate reset, reseed, derive the binding, commit the ledger, send reply op "reseeded" with commands_fenced true, then run serve_rewind; Disconnected loops for the next reset, Stopped returns and the guest powers off.

Inferred: JobCgroups is created once and reused across rewind sessions while JobCgroups.create allows 64 names per process (supervision.rs:128), so after 64 rewind jobs in total the next exec fails with the job-cgroup-name-consumed refusal and the guest powers off.
Helper refusals: "NUL in path", "root-owned non-writable directory required" (uid 0, directory, no group/other write), and "wrong guest filesystem" on an fstatfs magic mismatch.

cwd is empty (workspace root) or a relative path of at most 1024 bytes without leading '/' ("relative cwd required"); every component must be non-empty, not . or .., at most 255 bytes and free of control characters and DEL ("unsafe cwd component").
Jail wraps the pre-existing /sandbox and /sandbox/work descriptors built by bootstrap::prepare; it verifies them and resolves job cwds. It does not mount anything itself.

Jail::verify refusals: "unprivileged job identity required" for uid/gid 0, "unexpected jail root entry" for any /sandbox entry other than bin/etc/dev/proc/work, "jail base mount is not read-only", "unapproved guest device", "guest null device missing", "job proc cmdline must be masked" if /sandbox/proc/cmdline yields a byte, "private job workspace required" unless work is tmpfs owned 10000:10000 mode 0700, and "workspace tmpfs exceeds foundation ceiling" above 64 MiB.

Each cwd is re-resolved from the retained /sandbox descriptor: work must still have the same dev/inode, owner and mode 0700 ("workspace identity or permissions changed") and be tmpfs, and each component is opened with O_NOFOLLOW|O_DIRECTORY, so symlinks and non-directories fail.
Only character devices null 1:3, zero 1:5, random 1:8 and urandom 1:9 owned by root may exist in the jail /dev.
Builds the classic-BPF seccomp program installed in each job child by spawn::child_exec, using pinned libc ABI constants.
The child filter first checks seccomp_data.arch == AUDIT_ARCH_AARCH64 (0xc00000b7) and returns SECCOMP_RET_KILL_PROCESS for any other ABI.

38 syscalls return EPERM: unshare, setns, mount, umount2, pivot_root, chroot, ptrace, process_vm_readv/writev, bpf, perf_event_open, kcmp, pidfd_getfd, userfaultfd, io_uring_setup/register/enter, open_by_handle_at, name_to_handle_at, reboot, kexec_load, kexec_file_load, swapon, swapoff, init_module, finit_module, delete_module, fsopen, fsconfig, fsmount, open_tree, move_mount, mount_setattr, add_key, request_key, keyctl, capset, prctl.

clone3 returns ENOSYS to force the legacy clone fallback; socket and socketpair are allowed only for AF_UNIX (AF_VSOCK, AF_INET and others get EPERM); clone with any CLONE_NEW* namespace flag gets EPERM.
The final instruction is SECCOMP_RET_ALLOW, so the filter is a denylist: any syscall not listed is permitted to the job shell.

install_in_child refuses "filter size" for an empty program or more than 4096 instructions, then sets PR_SET_NO_NEW_PRIVS and installs the filter; it runs only in the fork child after chroot and credential drop.

Command is fixed /bin/sh -c <script> with environment exactly PATH=/bin, HOME=/work, TMPDIR=/work, LANG=C; script must be 1..=16384 UTF-8 bytes, stdin at most 49152, combined at most 65536 ("command/input bounds"), and no NUL ("command NUL").
Barrier enforces attach-then-release exactly once ("duplicate barrier attachment", "unattached/duplicate release"), so the child is released only after its PID is the sole member of its job cgroup.
Child owns one forked job shell (pid, gate, stdin, stdout, stderr, exec-error pipes) from fork until verified reaping; dispatch::Job holds it.

fork_blocked refuses "matching unprivileged identity required", "single-threaded broker required before fork" when /proc/self/task has more than one entry, and "broker stdio descriptors required" if fds 0-2 are not open; it creates gate, stdin, stdout, stderr and exec-error pipes and forks a child that waits on the gate.
attach_and_release writes the PID to cgroup.procs, records the barrier, then writes the single token '!' to the gate pipe; a missing gate refuses "barrier already consumed".

terminate closes stdin; if the gate was never released it just drops the gate (the child then fails its gate read and exits 126); otherwise it sends SIGTERM to the child's process group (-pid) unless the leader was reaped, ignoring ESRCH.
stdin is written nonblocking; EPIPE (the shell closed stdin) is treated as finished, not an error.

Child order: wait for gate token, setsid, dup stdio, fchdir+chroot(".") into /sandbox, fchdir to cwd, rlimits CORE 0, NOFILE 64, FSIZE 64 MiB, setgroups(0), clear KEEPCAPS, setresgid/setresuid 10000, clear signal mask, capset all zero, verify euid/egid, move exec-error pipe to fd 3 CLOEXEC, close_range(4..), seccomp, execve. Any failure writes EACCES to the exec-error pipe and _exit(126).
drain reads at most 16 x 4096 bytes (64 KiB) per call so a chatty child cannot starve timeout checks; returns true on EOF.
Job limits require guest memory 1..=256 MiB, job memory nonzero and below guest memory, and pids 1..=64 ("explicit bounded guest job limits required").

cgroup control reads are capped at 65536 bytes ("cgroup control exceeds bound"); writes open with O_NOFOLLOW and must pass filesystem(fd, CGROUP2_SUPER_MAGIC), otherwise the sandbox wrong-filesystem refusal.
JobCgroups/JobCgroup manage the root-owned /sys/fs/cgroup/terminal-jobs tree and per-job cgroups (limits, attach, kill, emptiness); used by dispatch and rewind.

prepare verifies proc, sysfs and cgroup2 magics, refuses "memory/pids controllers unavailable" if cgroup.controllers lacks memory or pids, enables +memory +pids, and creates /sys/fs/cgroup/terminal-jobs with the same subtree control.

At most 64 job cgroup names per broker process, never reused ("job cgroup name consumed"); each gets memory.max, memory.swap.max 0 and pids.max read back and cgroup.type domain checked ("job cgroup limits not applied"), and cgroup.kill must be openable.

attach requires pid > 1 ("child identity required") and cgroup.procs to then list exactly that PID ("unexpected cgroup members before child release"); kill_descendants writes 1 to cgroup.kill; empty() reads cgroup.events.
Emptiness needs exactly one 'populated ' line: 0 is empty, 1 is busy, anything else refuses "missing/duplicate populated witness".
Inferred from a crate-wide search: Completion and poll_job are only used by tests; dispatch::step_job checks the same closure witnesses inline.
Deadline needs timeout_ms 1..=60000 and now before session end ("invalid remaining job lifetime"), refuses "deadline overflow" on u64 overflow, and is clamped to the session end.
reap_available waits on every child (waitpid(-1, WNOHANG)) and reports whether ECHILD was reached, i.e. no children remain; as PID1 it also reaps reparented descendants.
Single nonblocking vsock connection with bounded framing and serialized writes; created by dispatch::serve (or Transport::rewound in the rewind profile).
QUEUE_MAX = 131072 bytes bounds the guest send queue.

Opens one nonblocking AF_VSOCK stream listener on VMADDR_CID_ANY port 19001 with backlog 1, polls every 25 ms until the lifetime end ("connection lifetime"), and accepts a single peer that must be CID 2 with a full sockaddr_vm ("host CID"). The listener is dropped on return, so no later connection can rebind the session.

receive() reads at most what the current frame needs in 4096-byte steps and refuses "frame/lifetime deadline" or "partial frame deadline" when the 3000 ms first-byte deadline or lifetime passes, and "connection EOF" when the host closes; header errors from Header::parse fire as soon as 24 bytes are buffered.

The Receiver is created from the first frame's own owner_id, so the owner check in Receiver is satisfied by construction; authentication rests on peer CID 2 plus the 64-hex boot nonce (comment line 171). A first frame that is not hello refuses "first frame not HELLO".

Every guest event is built from the bound ready metadata; supplying kind, workload_id, generation or reservation_id in the fields refuses "immutable event binding"; "HELLO required" when no sender exists yet.
enqueue() reserves HEADER + MAX_META + payload (24 + 4096 + n) against the 131072-byte queue ("send queue bound") and stamps each frame with a deadline of now + 3000 ms capped at lifetime end.

flush() writes up to 8 queued frames per call with MSG_NOSIGNAL; a frame still unsent at its deadline refuses "send deadline", a zero-byte send refuses "send zero". stdout_sent/stderr_sent advance only when the whole output frame has been written.
Per-job sent counters are reset only when the send queue is empty ("pending frames at new job"), so one job's bytes are never counted against the next.
Pure MVGC v1 framing and closed metadata validation with no socket or guest effects; used by transport.rs and, for identity grammar, by rewind.rs.
MVGC v1 limits: HEADER = 24 bytes, MAX_META = 4096 bytes, MAX_PAYLOAD = 65536 bytes, and integer fields capped at MAX_SAFE = 9007199254740991 (2^53-1).

Metadata must be 1..=4096 bytes ("metadata length") of a flat JSON object with scalar values only and no duplicate keys; any JSON error, nested array/object or duplicate key surfaces as "metadata JSON".

IDs are prefix + tail where prefixes are workload-, reservation-, request-, job-, actor-; the tail is 1..=64 bytes, starts with a lowercase letter or digit and contains only [a-z0-9._-]. Violations refuse "ID prefix" or "ID grammar"; wrong types refuse "string field" or "integer field".

Closed schema: every kind carries kind, workload_id, generation, reservation_id plus exactly its own fields (hello: nonce, owner_id, profile_id; exec: request_id, job_id, cwd, timeout_ms, command_bytes, stdin_bytes; cancel: request_id, run_request_id, job_id; stop/stopping: request_id; ready: none; accepted; output; job_finished; error). Unknown kind refuses "metadata kind"; missing or extra keys refuse "missing or unknown fields"; generation must be 1..=MAX_SAFE ("integer bounds").

hello requires owner_id actor-*, nonce of 64 lowercase hex ("nonce") and profile_id exactly "guest-command-arm64-v1" ("enum"). exec requires a safe relative cwd, timeout_ms 1..=60000, command_bytes 1..=16384 and stdin_bytes 0..=49152 ("integer bounds").

Guest event rules: accepted op in exec/cancel/stop and job_id null exactly when op is stop ("accepted job correlation"); output stream stdout/stderr and chunk_index 0..=65535; job_finished cause in exit/cancel/stop/timeout/output_limit, exactly one of exit_code 0..=255 or signal 1..=64 ("exclusive wait status"), job_empty true ("job not empty"), output_complete false iff cause output_limit ("lost output"), cancel/stop causes need their request id ("missing accepted control"), and stdout_sent_bytes + stderr_sent_bytes <= 65536 ("combined output").

error.code is limited to AUTH, PROTOCOL, BUSY, INVALID, DEADLINE, OUTPUT_LIMIT, RESOURCE, CLEANUP. Inferred from a crate-wide search: dispatch.rs only ever emits BUSY and INVALID; the other six are schema-valid but never sent by this guest.

Tags: hello 1, exec 2, cancel 3, stop 4, every guest event 5. exec payload length must equal command_bytes + stdin_bytes ("exec payload lengths") with UTF-8 command ("command UTF8") and no NUL ("command NUL"); output payload must be 1..=16384 bytes ("output chunk length"); every other kind must have an empty payload ("unexpected payload").

Header layout: bytes 0-3 "MVGC", byte 4 version 1, byte 5 tag 1..=5, bytes 6-7 zero (else "frame header"); bytes 8-11 big-endian metadata length 1..=4096, 12-15 payload length <= 65536, 16-23 big-endian u64 sequence nonzero (else "frame bounds"). Frame length = 24 + metadata + payload and is checked before any body allocation.

Frame decode refusals: "short header" under 24 bytes, "short or trailing frame bytes" when the buffer is not exactly the header length, and "tag/kind mismatch" when header tag disagrees with metadata kind.

Host-to-guest receiver: sequence starts at 1 and must increase by exactly one ("sequence gap/replay"); the first frame must be hello with the boot nonce and owner ("HELLO authentication") and binds the (workload_id, generation, reservation_id) tuple; later frames must keep that tuple and be exec, cancel or stop ("binding or direction"). Any error sets failed, after which every accept refuses "receiver fenced".

Exactly one Sender can be issued, only after an authenticated HELLO ("HELLO required"); a second request refuses "receiver fenced or writer already issued". The guest-to-host sequence is independent and also starts at 1.

Sender.encode accepts only tag-5 events carrying the bound tuple (else "event binding or direction"), consumes a sequence number per encoded frame, and fences itself ("sender fenced") on any error including "sequence exhausted", so a failed event is never retried.
A partially received frame must complete within 3000 ms of its first byte, capped at the lifetime end; with no byte pending the deadline is the lifetime end.

Opt-in rewind PID1 entry (feature rewind-profile): detect authority (else "rewind broker requires root ARM64 PID1", exit 78), then phases read_rewind_boot -> prepare -> rewind_serve. Its failure line "rewind_broker failed phase=... errno=... kind=..." carries no detail= field, so the refusal string is not printed; it always powers off and exits 78.
Binary rewind-command-broker: alternative PID1 for the opt-in ARM64 rewind profile, built only with feature rewind-profile.
The guest_command_event refused data.code enum is exactly INVALID, OWNER, BUSY, STALE, DUPLICATE, UNAVAILABLE, DEADLINE, CAPACITY.
The guest_command_event outcome_unknown data.code enum is exactly TRANSPORT, DEADLINE, PROCESS_IDENTITY, STORAGE, OUTPUT_LOSS, CLEANUP, PROTOCOL.
Run timeout_ms is limited to 1..60000 in the request schema.
Guest transport error frames carry code AUTH, PROTOCOL, BUSY, INVALID, DEADLINE, OUTPUT_LIMIT, RESOURCE or CLEANUP; the controller only maps BUSY/INVALID on a pending cancel into a public refusal.

host_path rejects trailing slashes, double slashes and '..'. Inferred: on a host whose own cgroup is '/', an external_cgroup of '/sys/fs/cgroup/' fails 'canonical absolute host path required'; this is what makes two rewind_runtime test_recovery loader tests error in this container [MEASURED].

Guest-command host config is a closed object: schema guest-command-host-config/v1, runtime_admitted boolean, owner_id actor-..., generation 1..2^53-1, startup_seconds/stop_seconds 1..30, canonical absolute runtime_root/external_cgroup, and exactly four artifacts engine/kernel/broker/busybox with path and lowercase sha256. ConfigError messages include 'unknown or missing configuration field' and 'deadline exceeds existing bounds'.

Controller is the single state writer inside the private service for one ARM64 Firecracker command guest (profile guest-command-arm64-v1). It is constructed by tools/guest_command_runner.py with the host config, core session ID, state dir and an emit callback that prints events to stdout for the Go manager.

_unknown sets phase uncertain/ownership held, marks a running job unknown, emits one outcome_unknown (on the pending request by priority run, stop, cancel, create, or on the create ID when idle) and always attempts a non-graceful native close in finally.

Every request is schema-validated first; if the evidence store reopened a non-empty journal, request raises Invalid('surviving state requires native reconciliation') instead of acting. A repeated request_id is refused DUPLICATE.

Create: BUSY if a session exists, UNAVAILABLE if runtime_admitted is false. Otherwise it builds session phase starting/ownership held (backend firecracker, isa aarch64), journals intent, emits accepted, opens the native VM, sends hello with the boot nonce, and needs a ready frame within startup_seconds; then emits ready and starts the reader. Any exception becomes outcome_unknown code TRANSPORT.

Refusal codes for run: UNAVAILABLE (no session), STALE (workload_id/generation mismatch or ownership released), BUSY (unknown state or phase not ready), DUPLICATE (job_id reused), CAPACITY (64 jobs), INVALID (prepare_exec rejected command/stdin/cwd bytes).

Cancel is refused BUSY unless an accepted run is in phase running with no prior cancel or stop, and STALE if job_id differs. Stop is refused BUSY if a stop was already requested; when the guest is already unknown, stop is accepted locally and closes the native VM without sending to the guest.

Guest frames are only accepted while held and known. accepted/output/job_finished/stopping must correlate to the current run or stop; job_finished needs matching control IDs, exactly one of exit_code/signal, job_empty true, output_complete unless cause output_limit, and exact stdout/stderr sent bytes ("lost output bytes"). A guest error frame is translated into a refused cancel only for codes BUSY or INVALID on a pending cancel; anything else raises "guest rejected dispatched operation".
Stopped is emitted only after native.close returns closed true (else Invalid('native absence unproved')), with session phase stopped, ownership released and data native_absent true.

The actor loop polls every 0.1 s; passing the native lifetime while held raises outcome_unknown code DEADLINE, a reader transport failure gives TRANSPORT, and any exception while handling a request or guest event gives PROTOCOL. On exit it always closes native, joins the reader for 4 s and closes the store.

Builds a deterministic gzip newc initramfs (mtime 0, root-owned) with the broker as /init (mode 0500), static busybox plus 48 applet symlinks, fixed directories and device nodes console/null/zero/urandom. Inputs must be static ARM64 ET_EXEC binaries (broker at most 12 MiB, busybox at most 4 MiB) or ImageError is raised.
NativeVM owns exactly one ARM64 Firecracker process and its runtime directory; it has no command semantics. A return from open means only that a raw vsock connection exists (module docstring).

The VM boots with mem_size_mib 256 and vcpu_count 1, guest CID 3, boot args including mv_guest_command=1 and a fresh 32-byte hex nonce, and a whole-VM lifetime of 55 seconds from boot (self.lifetime). Any failure during open closes non-gracefully and re-raises.

Runtime files are removed only if the directory keeps its device/inode and contains only fc, Image, initrd.gz, api.sock, vsock.sock; otherwise 'owned directory identity changed' or 'unknown runtime entry; retaining directory' and the directory is kept.

Graceful close requires the Firecracker process to exit 0 within stop_seconds ('guest poweroff failed'); otherwise pidfd SIGTERM then SIGKILL. The console drain thread must finish without error ('console drain closure unproved'); the console summary (last 4096 bytes, nonce redacted) is journaled.

Read-only custody and bounded native helpers copied from the accepted ARM harness (provenance mc04-runtime/arm_harness.py sha256 0ff103d8...). Constants: vsock PORT 19001, MEMORY 256 MiB, VCPUS 1, MAX_ASSET 128 MiB.

Assets are read O_NOFOLLOW, must be bounded regular files matching the explicit SHA-256; the kernel must be a raw ARM64 Linux Image (magic ARM\x64, little-endian 4K pages, image size within 256 MiB), other assets AArch64 ELF (machine 183), static ones without PT_DYNAMIC/PT_INTERP.
/dev/kvm must be a character device with KVM API version 12 and allow KVM_CREATE_VM; otherwise 'KVM is not a character device', 'KVM API is not 12' or 'KVM_CREATE_VM failed'.

The external cgroup must be a dedicated cgroup v2 path under /sys/fs/cgroup with no child cgroups, contain the harness itself, memory.max at most 512 MiB, pids.max at most 64, memory.swap.max 0, a cpu.max quota no larger than one CPU, and cgroup.procs exactly the harness plus the owned child. Messages include 'child cgroup present; descendant ownership unproved' and 'cgroup is not exclusively harness and owned child'.
available_memory reads MemAvailable and refuses below 1 GiB ('host MemAvailable below admission floor'); callers in native.py additionally require 32 GiB free.

Firecracker API calls are hand-written HTTP/1.1 PUTs over the API Unix socket with every receive bounded by one absolute deadline, headers under 8192 bytes, no transfer-encoding, body at most 4096 bytes, and success only on status 204 with an empty body ('API <path>: <status> ...').
Cleanup signals only through the retained pidfd (or the owning Popen): SIGTERM, wait timeout, then SIGKILL and wait again; 'owned process not reaped' if it is still alive.
The runtime root must be an owned 0700 directory and its resolved path at most 70 bytes ('runtime root too long for Unix sockets'), the reason the Go side uses short prefixes.

Python reservation_id must equal the Go reservationID: domain tag MetaViewer/guest-command/reservation/v1 NUL, 4-byte big-endian length + session UTF-8 (1..128 chars, at most 512 bytes), 4-byte length + ASCII request_id.

A run request becomes an exec frame only if cwd is a relative workspace path, command_utf8 is 1..16384 bytes with no NUL, stdin_b64 decodes canonically to at most 49152 bytes, workload/generation match the binding, and the metadata JSON is at most 4096 bytes. Failures raise Invalid, which the controller refuses as INVALID.

The validator accepts only a frozen JSON Schema subset ($ref, oneOf, const, enum, closed objects, integer/string/boolean/null); every object must have additionalProperties false. Unsupported keywords raise 'unsupported schema keyword'.

Frame kind numbers are fixed: hello 1, exec 2, cancel 3, stop 4, and ready/accepted/output/job_finished/stopping/error all 5. Exec payload length must equal command_bytes+stdin_bytes; output payload 1..16384 bytes; every other frame has no payload.

Store is the single-writer, hash-chained, fsynced private journal (journal.jsonl plus owner.lock flock) for one controller. Reopening a non-empty journal sets recovery_required, so surviving evidence is inspection-only; errors include 'partial journal; explicit reconciliation required', 'invalid journal chain', 'journal digest mismatch', 'configuration changed', 'unaccounted evidence in fresh directory'.
Each journal row is at most 32768 bytes and the journal at most 8 MiB ('journal budget exhausted'); any write failure poisons the store.
Raw output chunks are 1..16384 bytes, strictly ordered per stream, at most 65536 bytes per job and 4 MiB per store ('output order or budget exceeded'); each chunk is fsynced before it is published.
Metadata is validated before any byte is written; a failed or timed-out partial write poisons the connection and is never retried.

MVGC frames: 24-byte header (magic MVGC, version 1, kind 1..5, flags 0, metadata length 1..4096, payload at most 65536, sequence starting at 1 and strictly incrementing). Once the first byte of a frame arrives it must complete within 3 seconds (partial_seconds); any error poisons the connection permanently ('connection is terminal').

Holdings ground truth must have source "holdings_lane", a 64-hex state_sha256 and tick <= 9007199254740991 (MaxHoldingsTick); an optional state is capped at 1 MiB (MaxHoldingsStateBytes) and must pass the strict state validator.

Holdings state JSON must be valid UTF-8, a top-level object, at most 1 MiB, with no trailing bytes; the hand-written validator rejects duplicate keys, depth > 64, floats/exponents, leading zeros and integers above 2^53-1.

Every malformed Holdings observe reply (oversize, multi-line, unknown fields, bad state_sha256/tick/revision/frame_state_sha256/elements, or both state and observation present) becomes fault code "malformed_cli"; Manager.input then simply omits GroundTruth instead of failing the input.

Defines the surface_request wire shape (Request{schema,op,params}), the surface_event/v0.1 error event and the Backend interface that the daemon dispatches capsule operations through; Manager is the real Backend.

An error event requires a non-empty surface_id up to 128 bytes, a fault code up to 128 bytes and a detail up to 65536 bytes; otherwise it fails with "error event requires supplied surface identity and fault" and no synthetic identity is invented.
New() returns a skeleton Backend that refuses every request with code "configuration" and detail "native profile and session configuration required"; runtime capsules need NewManager/NewRuntime.

egress.go stores per-identity browser egress records at <state>/egress/<profile>.json (schema metaviewer.capsule_egress/v1); a missing record means open, a malformed one never does; 64 KiB per file and 256 hostnames max [CITED: egress.go:5].
Egress mode must be open with zero domains or allowlisted with 1-256 domains (else "NET_EGRESS_INVALID"); every domain must be a unique lowercase exact ASCII hostname (else "NET_DOMAIN_INVALID").

Hostnames must contain a dot, be <=253 chars, lowercase, not an IP or hex/numeric form, not localhost/local/internal/lan/home.arpa (or their subdomains), with labels 1-63 chars of a-z0-9- not starting or ending with -.
The egress directory is walked with held descriptors and O_NOFOLLOW from /; the state dir and egress dir must be current-uid mode 0700, otherwise EACCES.

LoadEgress fails "NET_EGRESS_INVALID" for an invalid identity, unknown fields or trailing JSON, and "NET_EGRESS_IO" for directory/file permission, size or link problems; ENOENT yields the open default.

Egress writes are atomic (O_EXCL temp + fsync + renameat + dir fsync) and refuse to replace an existing link, special or wrongly-permissioned file ("NET_EGRESS_IO"); oversize documents fail "NET_EGRESS_INVALID".
After publishing policy the record is re-read; any change fails "NET_EGRESS_CHANGED" ("egress record changed during network preparation") so a stale policy never starts.

browserNetwork chooses the browser start network mode: allowlisted records need proxied and fail "NET_PROXIED_UNSUPPORTED" ("trusted capability declaration lacks proxied" or "allowlisted egress requires native runner"); open records use open if declared, else legacy; proxied writes the browserid.proxy-policy/v1 file.
Start argv gains --net open or --net proxied --policy <file>; proxied without a policy or an unknown mode fails "NET_EGRESS_INVALID".
For open/proxied starts a per-call runner copy strips SRF_EGRESS_PROXY from the child environment; shared runner env is never mutated.

Proxied starts append --proxy-bin <bin>/srf-egress-proxy (missing executable is a pre-spawn "NET_EGRESS_INVALID"); an open start exiting 3 (setup) becomes "NET_OPEN_PREREQ" naming the required identity image rebuild and root-owned firewall witness.

egress_started.go writes adapter-local start evidence <profile>.started.json (schema metaviewer.capsule_egress_started/v1, mode 0400) freezing effective mode, record sha256 (or "absent") and start times; no wire fields are added.
The started record is removed before each browser start and after a verified browser stop; a missing directory or file is success.
handoff.go implements legacy take_control/release_control between agent and human on agent-role surfaces, single-use input permits and the drain handshake.

take_control/release_control refuse "surface" ("active surface required"), "POLICY" ("surface is draining", "human capsule role is immutable", "human takeover requires agent ownership", "takeover input must be drained before release"). Takeover cancels in-flight inputs and bumps the epoch; release bumps the epoch and sets the refresh fence so agent input needs a fresh capture.
RequireFrameRefresh raises the refresh fence and FrameRefreshEpoch for active agent-controlled, non-human surfaces; otherwise "POLICY" ("state refresh requires active agent control").

A cancelled input stays in pending until the owner calls DrainInput after native completion; until then release_control, destroy, capture and login are blocked. Wrong calls fail "POLICY" ("completed cancelled input required").
Only the exact native diagnostic "resized: WxH -> WxH" (optionally prefixed host_window_unavailable:) with target sides 1..4096 counts as a resize; resize is capture progress, not absence.

Loss classification is substring-based on lowercase error text: minimized/iconic/unmapped are never terminal, while any text containing host_window_unavailable:, witness, closed, no such window, badwindow, baddrawable, destroyed, not found or gone marks the surface lost.

Only big-endian 32-bpp ZPixmap XWD (version 7, format 2) with header 100..4096 bytes, width/height 1..4096, bytes_per_line 4w..4w+64 and <=256 colors is decoded to RGB24; others fail "invalid XWD header" or "truncated XWD pixels".

host_window.go attaches an existing window of the person's own X11 session (srf-hw-<profile>-<xid>) or a host-xpra window as a desktop_capsule, captures it via srf-host-window capture (XWD) and drives input via srf-host-window input; the program stays on the host and is never isolated.

A host-window binding always starts with Role agent and Control agent, Window w1, run id run-hw-<16 hex>, frames under <RAMRoot>/<run>/frames/w1 (mode 0700); collisions fail "binding", directory errors fail "configuration" ("failed to allocate/secure host-window frames directory").

Capture outcomes: resize diagnostic -> "host_window_resized" with geometry updated; minimized/iconic/unmapped -> "host_window_unavailable" waiting (HostMinimized set, surface stays active); closed/witness/BadWindow/gone -> surface marked lost with pendingHostLost and "host_window_unavailable"; undecodable output -> "frame" ("invalid host window XWD frame").

Host window input supports click, key and type only (scroll and others are "unsupported"); host-xpra keys add --key-hold-ms 80; type is split into 2000-rune --type calls; MV_INPUT_DIAGNOSTICS=1 prints METAVIEWER_HOST_INPUT stage lines without input data.

A host-window ack must be {ok:true, xid, witness, kind, focus_verified:true} matching the bound XID, witness and action (text expected as type), else "input" ("unverified host-window input receipt"); a terminal refusal marks the surface lost and returns "host_window_unavailable".

Resize updates surface geometry for host-window/host-xpra and windowed browser/program bindings; only host-window kinds also rewrite the profile size, identity profiles keep their configured allocation.
MarkHostWindowLost / BeginHostWindowLost let the capture tap declare a host-window or host-xpra surface lost with a reason; other kinds fail "surface" ("host-window surface required").

host_xpra.go runs a Host program (host-exec opening with host_xpra) on the host inside a private Xvfb display served by xpra, so the wall can show it; it is not an isolated capsule: the program runs as the host user with RAM-only HOME/XDG dirs.

stop signals the Xvfb process group only if /proc/<pid>/stat start time and group still match the recorded witness (else "host_program_unavailable" "stale process witness: no signal sent"); SIGTERM, 2 s wait, SIGKILL, then reap and fail "recorded group removal unverified" if any member survives 1 s more; finally removes view and RAM root.
The xpra child command is single-quoted for shlex (no shell); chromium/chrome get --user-data-dir in the RAM root and firefox gets --no-remote --profile in the RAM root.

Readiness polls the X/xpra sockets every 50 ms within a 20 s budget; if the child becomes a zombie it fails "host_program_unavailable" ("<label> exited before socket readiness: <log tail>"), on timeout "private display/socket readiness timed out".

startHostXpra requires xpra, Xvfb, xauth, xdotool and srf-host-window, creates /dev/shm/mv-host-xpra-* (browser, config, cache, data, runtime) plus <state>/view/<container>/s, writes a private Xauthority cookie, starts Xvfb at a random display :10000-:59999 with 1280x900x24, then xpra start-desktop bound to a 0600 unix socket and a 127.0.0.1 TCP port with html on and clipboard, audio, printing, dbus, mdns off.

A missing tool fails "host_program_unavailable" with "host_program_unavailable: <name> missing; install xpra xvfb xauth xdotool (apt install xpra xvfb xauth xdotool)" or "host_program_unavailable: srf-host-window missing" (UI code HOST_PROGRAM_UNAVAILABLE); these are pre-spawn so the reservation is released.

Role is fixed at start: xpra is launched with --readonly=true for agent role and --readonly=false for human role, so a role change of a host-xpra Host program cannot be applied in place (SwitchRole refuses it) and requires a new start.

createHostXpra reserves the profile in quarantine, drops mu during native startup, polls srf-host-window list every 100 ms for up to 15 s for a visible normal non-minimized window owned by the Xvfb process group whose XID and witness are identical in two consecutive inventories, resizes it to 1280x900 at 0,0, then attaches it as a host-window binding with NativeKind host-xpra and container srf-pg-hx-<profile>.

The profile stays quarantined across the unlocked startup; it is released only on a preSpawnRefusal or when the compensating process.stop succeeds, so a failed stop leaves the profile counted against capacity.

Host program start fails "host_program_unavailable" with "host_program_unavailable: program exited before publishing an X11 window" or "host_program_unavailable: program did not publish an X11 window on its private display"; non-process runners fail "configuration" ("host-xpra requires process runner").

Window layout uses xdotool windowsize 1280 900 and windowmove 0 0 on the private display; failure is "host_program_unavailable" ("host_program_unavailable: private window layout failed" or "xdotool missing").
publishHumanBinding is the witness the UI host reads to open the human view; control_ready is true only when the surface is active with no pending input. Fake runners skip it.

For browser, host-exec program and host-xpra bindings with an identity-pattern container, the runner atomically writes <state>/human-bindings/<surface_id>.json (schema metaviewer.human_binding/v0.3: surface_id, container, run_id, control_ready, input_epoch, width, height, role, profile_id, host_xpra); the dir must be 0700 else "binding" ("human binding directory unavailable" / "private human binding directory required").
Profile ids starting with srf-id-cuentas-, srf-id-perplexity- or srf-pg- are protected and refused everywhere (create, slots, identity checks).

identity_profiles.go turns saved identities into dynamic profiles: the first sorted 1280x900 browser profile is the template, and a logical display pool expanded up to MaxSurfaces is allocated per opening.

ProfileFor is routing information only; it never returns static profiles (the daemon keeps its own admission map). profileFor falls back to a 1280x900 host-window profile for hw- ids when no browser template exists.

A Host program profile is derived from the identity template as desktop_capsule/program/host-exec, role agent, depth 0, no display; it requires a stored-identity id ^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]{1,39}$ that is not protected.
Host program (host-exec) admission refuses "profile": "host-exec requires dynamic program profile", "program profile refused", "identity display pool exhausted; stop a capsule first".

Host-window admission refuses "profile" ("host-window requires dynamic window profile", "host-window profile refused"), spec validation errors, and "host_window_unavailable" ("window already attached; if its tile shows Window Closed, press Stop on that tile and add the window again") when the XID is already bound.

Identity admission refuses "profile" ("configured display is in use; stop its capsule first", "identity refused", "identity display pool exhausted; stop a capsule first") and "identity_unavailable" ("identity must exist in the configured store") when srf-identity-admin show cannot confirm the id.
Dynamic profiles are dropped from cfg.Profiles once not quarantined and no non-destroyed binding uses them, freeing their display slot.
Identity existence is checked only through srf-identity-admin show --id <id>; a mismatched profile_id fails "profile" ("identity metadata mismatch"); browser profile files are never opened.
Only native fault codes "unavailable" and "refused" count as a liveness miss; deadlines, cli_failed, malformed, setup and usage break the consecutive-miss run and never prove loss.

MonitorLiveness runs a ticker (default 5 s) that probes each active or unconfirmed-lost native capsule with the frame verb; host-window and host-xpra are not probed. A failed emit ends the session; misconfiguration fails "configuration" ("configured liveness monitor required").

After LivenessMisses (default 2) consecutive absence faults an active capsule becomes lost via markLostLocked and state_changed(lost) is emitted; a lost-by-stop capsule only gains ConfirmedAbsent. A valid bound frame clears a recoveryProbe token from an undelivered lost event.

Agent input is refused "LOGIN_ACTIVE" while a login is opening in this manager ("operator login blocks agent input") or when <state>/views/<container>.pid or .login-pending exists or cannot be checked ("operator login registration blocks agent input").

Config carries Profiles, BinDir, MaxSurfaces, MaxOutputBytes, Timeout, OriginNS, liveness knobs, optional View backend, Inventory custody, NetModes, BeforeDestroy drain hook and the Holdings verifier hooks VerifyHoldingsInput/VerifyHoldingsRemoval.

Human text uses srf --paste only when it contains a rune outside 0x20-0x7E (xdotool type drops non-ASCII, paste costs about 1.7 s per call [CITED: manager.go:165-166]); WheelStepPx=50 and ScrollMaxSteps=20 [CITED: manager.go:172-173].

Manager is the single in-process authority for capsule lifecycle: it holds bindings, quarantine, pending creates, in-flight inputs, input epochs, login locks, views and dynamic profiles under one mutex mu, and shells out to native srf-* CLIs for start/stop/frame/input.

WireCode maps internal lowercase faults to the uppercase UI wire: binding+"profile already bound" -> PROFILE_ALREADY_BOUND, uncertain+capacity detail -> SURFACE_CAPACITY_OR_QUARANTINE, identity_unavailable -> IDENTITY_UNAVAILABLE, host_program_unavailable -> HOST_PROGRAM_UNAVAILABLE, host_window_unavailable -> HOST_WINDOW_UNAVAILABLE; codes already uppercase (POLICY, LOGIN_ACTIVE, NET_*) pass through; other faults become ADAPTER_<CODE>; non-Fault errors ADAPTER_ERROR.

Native start exit status 4 surfaces as IDENTITY_UNAVAILABLE with detail telling the operator the identity may be held by a live capsule or an abandoned lease, that the adapter cannot reclaim a lease, and to close the holder or recover the lease out of band before retrying.
desktop_capsule programs are admitted only as "notepad", "metaviewer-nested" or per-create "host-exec" at nested_depth 0, or "metaviewer-nested" at nested_depth 1; nested_depth > 1 is refused.

NewManager refuses with code "configuration" ("complete bounded native configuration required") unless runner/clock are set, OriginNS != 0, BinDir is absolute, MaxSurfaces >= 1, MaxOutputBytes in 1..1<<20, Timeout in (0, 3m] and at least one profile; liveness defaults are 5s interval, 2 misses, timeout min(Timeout, 2s).

Startup profile validation refuses with code "configuration" and details: "invalid native network capability declaration", "invalid default mode", "invalid capsule role", "human role requires 1280x900 browser", "invalid text input mode", "invalid profile geometry or allocation", "nested profile requires 1280x720 desktop_capsule", "browser mapping invalid", "program mapping required", "virtual program mapping required", "game application mapping required", "unsupported public kind", "distinct profile displays required".

Public kind maps to exactly one native kind: browser->browser (no program), desktop_capsule->program with an admitted program (static host-exec refused), vm->vm with a profile-id program, game_capsule->holdings with an absolute AppDir; RAMRoot must be /dev/shm or under it (withinRAM).

execute refuses protected containers first, picks srf-identity-surface, srf-holdings-capsule (holdings) or srf-host-window (host-window), applies cfg.Timeout, swaps in a network-mode runner for browser starts, and rejects output over MaxOutputBytes with "malformed_cli"/"native output exceeds cap".

Quarantine release proof reads <SRF_IDENTITY_STORE_ROOT>/locks/<profile>.json (regular, mode 0600, current uid, nlink 1, <=4096 bytes, active:false, holder srf-id-*), requires no login view, a unix:// docker context and no docker container named as the holder; any doubt returns false and keeps quarantine.
HandleInputWithEvidence is the input entry that also returns request-local native evidence; any op other than input is refused with code "input" ("input request required for evidence").

handle accepts schema surface_request/v0.1 or v0.2 (else fault "schema"/"unsupported request schema"), takes mu, and dispatches create, list, destroy, input, take_control/release_control, view/login/view-stop; frame_subscribe, frame_unsubscribe, record_start, record_stop return code "unsupported"; any other op returns "unknown_op".

view/login/view-stop refuse: "usage" ("surface_id required" or "invalid identity capsule" for holdings, host-window and host-xpra), "unsupported" when no View backend, "surface" ("active surface required"), "refused" ("view unavailable or already registered"), "POLICY" ("input must drain before operator login") and "LOGIN_ACTIVE" ("operator login is already opening").

View.Open/Stop run outside mu; on native error the login lock is deliberately kept (only a verified stop reopens agent admission). If the binding changed meanwhile, the view is stopped with a detached timeout and "surface" is returned.

create parses {kind, profile_id, geometry, nested_depth}; nested_depth outside 0..1 or on a non-desktop_capsule is fault "nested_depth"; profile ids with protected prefixes are refused with "protected_container" ("protected identity refused").

For a dynamic desktop_capsule the runner's private opening request is consumed in order: host-xpra (ConsumeOpeningHostXpra), then Host program (ConsumeOpeningProgramMode, binary resolved via ResolveHostBinary), then host-window (ConsumeOpeningWindow); a non-process runner presenting such a request for a static profile is refused with "profile" ("host-exec requires dynamic program profile" / "host-window requires dynamic window profile").

Profile admission refuses with code "profile" ("unadmitted profile, kind or geometry", "unadmitted host-xpra profile") when kind or requested geometry differ from the profile, and with "nested_depth" ("profile nested_depth mismatch"); host-window opening geometry must be 1..4096 per side.

Before any native call the profile-derived container (srf-id-, srf-pg-, srf-hw-, srf-vm- + profile) is checked against the protected container list, except for browsers, whose native names are random.

Capacity counts quarantined profiles plus every non-destroyed binding (lost included). A second create for a bound profile fails "binding"/"profile already bound" (PROFILE_ALREADY_BOUND); reaching MaxSurfaces or a quarantined profile fails "uncertain"/"surface capacity or unresolved native outcome" (SURFACE_CAPACITY_OR_QUARANTINE). A quarantined browser profile is released only if releasedIdentityAbsent proves the lease inactive and the container absent.

Dynamic profile admission: host-xpra records a display-less dynamic profile; host-window, host-exec and identity profiles call their admit functions; then the opening mode is consumed. A human mode outside 1280x900 browser or 1280x900 depth-0 Host program (program/host-xpra host-exec) fails "configuration" ("human mode requires 1280x900 browser").

Browser start freezes the egress record digest; failures are "NET_EGRESS_IO" (snapshot read), egress errors from browserNetwork, and "NET_EGRESS_CHANGED" ("egress record changed during start preparation") when the record changed before start.

Quarantine is set before native start and a pendingCreate (generation, kind, slot 1, predicted container) is recorded; Inventory.Pending is called and Inventory.Unknown on any later error. Only a preSpawnRefusal (proof nothing was spawned) clears quarantine immediately.
A native "unavailable" fault (exit 4) on a non-Holdings start is rewritten to "identity_unavailable" with detailIdentityUnavailable; quarantine is retained because absence is unproven.

On a failed create, cleanup stops the native capsule only if the reply named a syntactically valid container/run_id correlated by pendingCleanup and not owned by another binding; a verified stop clears quarantine, otherwise the profile stays quarantined and a non-native error is wrapped as "uncertain" ("profile <id> remains quarantined after failed create: ...").

Readiness validation returns "malformed_cli": "one game capsule required" and "invalid game readiness or binding" for Holdings (slot 1, container pattern, exact display/geometry, ready_line, ready_ms, frames_dir under RAMRoot), "invalid identity readiness or binding" for identity starts (one window w1 within profile geometry, matching kind).

A new binding must not reuse any live run_id, frames root (or nested frames root) or container; collisions fail "binding" ("native run or frame allocation already observed" / "native container already observed") and drop cleanup authority so foreign native files are never removed.

After readiness: the egress started record and allowlist policy are rebound to the real container, Control is "human" for human role, Role defaults to "agent", Inventory.Bound is called, the human binding file is published, then the binding is stored, quarantine cleared and surface_event created emitted.

destroy refuses "surface" ("unknown or terminal surface", "destroy already in progress") and "POLICY" ("input must be drained before destroy"); it drains capture subscribers outside mu, stops any view, sets state lost, and only after stopNative succeeds marks destroyed and releases quarantine, login lock, epochs and refresh fence.
If View.Stop or stopNative fails, the binding is left in state "lost" (capacity still consumed) and the native error is returned; a later destroy can retry.

Removal proof: reply must be {stopped:<container>} with removed_verified true (required for non-Holdings); Holdings additionally needs VerifyHoldingsRemoval or fails "uncertain" ("independent Holdings removal proof required"); bad replies fail "malformed_cli" ("native removal was not verified"). An "unavailable" stop is accepted only when absence was already confirmed.

host-xpra stop kills the private Xvfb/xpra process group then only removes RAM frames; host-window stop never signals anything (detachHostWindowLocked just deletes the RAM run dir), because the window belongs to the user's own host program. The second branch's host-xpra test at 1261 is unreachable.

After a verified program stop the adapter removes <RAMRoot>/<run_id> only if it is a real directory under the root owned by the current uid; violations fail "configuration" ("native RAM run directory outside root", "native RAM root invalid", "native RAM run directory invalid", "native RAM run directory owner mismatch").

Capture refuses "host_window_unavailable" with the pending loss reason, "surface" ("capture requires an active surface"), "POLICY" ("input must be drained before capture") if input ran during the frame, "frame" ("native frame allocation mismatch" / "native frame identity, time or allocation mismatch") when path, seq, generation, geometry, digest or capture_mono_ns window disagree.

active -> lost requires confirmed absence; it cancels every pending input on the surface and returns state_changed(lost). A second call with an already-confirmed host loss returns the stashed pendingHostLost event once. Otherwise "surface" ("confirmed active disappearance required").

If the lost event was not delivered, the binding rolls back to active with a recoveryProbe token; input, capture and subscriptions stay refused until a later liveness frame probe proves the capsule live.

Input admission refusals in order: "input" ("invalid input origin"), "surface" ("input identity required"), "POLICY" ("surface is draining"), "POLICY" ("human role excludes native input"), "LOGIN_ACTIVE" for agent input during operator login, "SURFACE_NOT_HUMAN_CONTROLLED" / "SURFACE_NOT_AGENT_CONTROLLED", and "POLICY" ("fresh frame and unused input permit required") for a refresh fence, pending input, reused proposal_id or >=100000 used permits.
A binding whose Role is "human" (human-mode browser or Host program, including host-xpra) never accepts adapter input of either origin; the person drives it directly through the native view.

Action lowering: click needs left/middle/right and x,y inside geometry; key needs 1-8 keys joining to ^[A-Za-z0-9_+]{1,32}$; type needs printable text, <=16384 runes (else "TEXT_TOO_LONG"), chunked at 2000 runes, --paste for profile text_input paste (agent) or non-ASCII human text; scroll only for human origin on non-Holdings, dominant axis, 50 px per step, 1-20 steps. Violations fail "input" ("invalid click", "invalid key", "invalid key chord", "invalid text", "text must contain printable runes", "invalid scroll"); other actions "unsupported".

Each native call runs outside mu under a cancellable context registered in m.pending; after it, a takeover yields "SURFACE_NOT_AGENT_CONTROLLED" ("input cancelled by control takeover"), a changed binding yields "surface" ("surface lost during input"), native "refused" result yields "refused" ("native input refused"), and a receipt with input_mono_ns outside [before, after] or missing window/focus proof yields "input" ("unverified input receipt").

Holdings input must return only input_mono_ns and requires VerifyHoldingsInput, else "input" ("independent Holdings input proof required"); for agent input with evidence it runs observe before and after and attaches GroundTruth only when both parse and agree on state presence.

Evidence is written only after all checks pass; a verified scroll omits kind because contracts/v0.2 action_receipt native_evidence.kind admits only click|key|text. Success emits surface_event input_applied {surface_id, proposal_id}.

HandleFor converts any failure into a surface_event error carrying the caller's reserved correlation id (else "correlation"); a non-Fault error becomes "native_failed" ("native operation has no verified result"); the error event code is the internal lowercase code, schema v0.2 when the request was v0.2.
A start reply's net_mode must be empty, legacy or one declared in cfg.NetModes, else "malformed_cli" ("undeclared network mode in identity start").

The UI host stages a one-shot private file <state>/opening-modes/<profile>.json (schema metaviewer.opening_mode/v0.3, mode human|agent, optional host_binary, host_xpra, host_window); the adapter consumes and deletes it at create. Directory must be 0700 and file 0600, current uid, <=2048 bytes.

Opening request refusals are "configuration": "invalid opening profile", "private opening directory required", "private opening request required", "opening mode refused", "host-xpra opening requires host program target"; a missing file keeps the legacy default.
A host window opening must be agent mode with no host_binary; otherwise "configuration" ("opening mode refused"). Host windows can therefore never be opened in human mode.

Host window specs need a nonzero XID and a 1-128 char printable witness without shell metacharacters; failures are "host_window_unavailable" with "invalid xid or witness", "invalid window metadata", "invalid X11 session" or "invalid window geometry".

Host program binaries resolve without a shell: absolute clean executable paths or bare names found in the runner PATH; failures are "host_program_unavailable" with "binary name is required", "invalid binary name", "path must be clean", "not found or not executable", "relative path refused", "not found in PATH".
A host_xpra opening without a binary or with a host_window fails "configuration" ("host-xpra binary required").

ProcessRunner is the trusted execution seam: it runs only admitted srf-* binaries from MV_SRF_BIN_DIR with a fixed environment allowlist, serializes srf-identity-surface calls through nativeGate, and classifies failures.

Only PATH, HOME, XDG_RUNTIME_DIR, MV_SRF_STATE_DIR, SRF_IDENTITY_STORE_ROOT, SRF_PROXY_REGISTRY and SRF_EGRESS_PROXY are admitted; PATH is mandatory; violations fail "configuration" ("bounded process configuration required", "unadmitted process environment", "explicit process search path required").

MV_SRF_STATE_DIR must be an absolute clean directory owned by the current uid with mode exactly 0700, rechecked before every identity verb; else "configuration" ("MV_SRF_STATE_DIR must be a current-uid directory with mode 0700").

Before a frame call the runner probes <state>/control.lock with a non-blocking shared flock; if held (native recorder/demo sealing) it returns pre-spawn "native_busy" ("native control lock held"); invalid lock files give "configuration".
preSpawnRefusal marks errors proven to occur before exec; it is the only evidence allowed to clear a create quarantine, a generic configuration fault is not.

Run refuses "execution" ("unadmitted executable") for any binary outside the bin dir or not in the admitted set (srf-identity-surface, srf-holdings-capsule, srf-host-window list/capture/input, srf-identity-admin show/create in exact shapes); queue wait timeout is pre-spawn "timeout"; a caller-supplied --state-dir is "configuration" ("state directory flag is adapter-owned").

Each native call gets its own process group (Setpgid) and cancellation kills the whole group with SIGKILL; stdout is capped at the configured limit and stderr at min(limit, 4096) bytes; WaitDelay 1 s.

srf-host-window capture streams stdout and reads exactly one XWD frame, then kills the group; a failed read is classified from stderr/out sample into pre-spawn "host_window_unavailable" faults, ending with "host_window_unavailable: invalid or truncated XWD capture".

Exit handling: deadline/cancel -> "uncertain" ("native command deadline or cancellation"); srf-identity-surface exit 2 with host_program_unavailable: text -> pre-spawn "host_program_unavailable"; srf-host-window failures -> "host_window_unavailable"; otherwise cli.ExitFault (2 usage, 3 setup, 4 unavailable, 5 malformed, 6 refused, 7 cli_failed) with the first stderr line appended.

NewRuntime reads MV_SRF_BIN_DIR, MV_SRF_LIVE_PROFILE, optional MV_LIVENESS_INTERVAL (Go duration > 0) and MV_LIVENESS_MISSES (int > 0); invalid explicit values fail "configuration" ("invalid MV_LIVENESS_INTERVAL" / "invalid MV_LIVENESS_MISSES") instead of defaulting.

Any argv with --container/-container/--capsule/-capsule naming srf-id-cuentas-1, srf-id-perplexity-1, srf-pg-notepad-1, srf-pg-metaviewer-1, srf-egress-proxy, n8n or distil-box is refused "protected_container" ("native operation refused for protected container <name>") before any exec.

Create cleanup authority comes only from the process-local pendingCreate generation and kind; the container must be unprotected, unbound, and match the Holdings pattern with slot 1 or the identity pattern ^srf-(id|pg|vm)-.
AdmissionProfiles returns every quarantined profile plus every profile with a non-destroyed (including lost) binding, the same reservation set that create counts against MaxSurfaces.

Resident ring capture refuses "host_window_unavailable" for pending host loss, "surface" ("resident capture requires active drained surface"), "POLICY" ("resident capture binding changed") if input or a refresh ran during read, and "ring_wire" ("resident capture clock outside session") when capture_mono_ns precedes OriginNS or follows the read.
A hostile resident writer quarantines the profile, marks the surface lost and stops the native capsule; only a verified stop clears quarantine and marks it destroyed.

SwitchRole is the host-only human/agent role conversion behind metaviewer.role_switch/v0.3; it changes Role and Control in place without starting or stopping native runtime, bumps input and frame epochs, republishes the human binding and raises the refresh fence.

Refusals are all "POLICY" (reaching the UI as code POLICY in role_switch_result): "invalid opening role", "role switch requires active drained surface", "native role switch unsupported" (vm, holdings, host-window, host-xpra and non-host-exec programs), "opening role unproven", "role epoch exhausted".

Only browser and in-capsule host-exec program bindings can switch role in place; a host-xpra Host program is refused because its xpra readonly flag is fixed at start (Inferred: the UI host restarts it with a new opening request instead).
If publishing the human binding fails the input epoch is restored and the binding left unchanged; the publish error (e.g. "binding") is returned.

Slot store init needs SRF_IDENTITY_STORE_ROOT and a local docker image opensuperficies-identity-browser-<x64|arm64>:0.2.0 or 0.1.1 (never pulled); failures SLOT_ARCHITECTURE_UNSUPPORTED or SLOT_HELPER_IMAGE_ABSENT disable slots only, not capture.

Slot custody requires the identity to be stopped: IDENTITY_BOUND (bound, quarantined, active lease or running docker container srf-id-/srf-pg-/srf-vm-<id>), LOGIN_IN_PROGRESS (login marker), CUSTODY_UNPROVEN (non-process runner, unreadable lease, docker error).

HandleState serves capsule_state_request/v0.2 (list, save, overwrite, load, delete, copy of saved identity slots) and always returns capsule_state_event/v0.2 with event completed or refused plus reason_code; causes are logged, never sent.

State refusal reason codes: POLICY (bad schema, ids, protected or live profile, missing credential_copy_confirmed, unknown op), SLOT_STORE_UNAVAILABLE or the init error, FOREIGN_IDENTITY (admin metadata mismatch), FOREIGN_SLOT, IDENTITY_PROTECTED (bad copy destination), IDENTITY_CREATION_UNAVAILABLE; other errors map via stateReason to their uppercase prefix, SLOT_NOT_FOUND or SLOT_OPERATION_FAILED.
Native admin browser "chromium" or "browser" maps to slot kind browser and "program" to program; copy creates the destination with srf-identity-admin create (--browser program only for program).
stateDirInfo walks a path from / with O_NOFOLLOW descriptors, creating only the final component with mode 0700; any symlink component fails, and callers still check owner and exact mode.

Package slots stores stopped capsule data (not open tabs or process state) as named slots with A/B references and generations; adapter-only API, callers must hold core authority. HumanConfirmed means an explicit click acknowledging that signed-in sessions travel. No power-loss claim is made for btrfs or WSL2.

New refuses "SLOT_CONFIGURATION_REQUIRED" (root not absolute, no image or no CheckStopped), "UNSAFE_PATH" (comma or newline, or symlinked root), "SLOT_QUOTA" (MaxBytes < 1), "UNSAFE_DIRECTORY" (root, profiles, metadata, locks not 0700 owned). DefaultMaxBytes is 4<<30 [TARGET] total retained slot bytes.
Slot metadata reads require a regular 0600 file owned by the effective user and <= 65536 bytes ("UNSAFE_METADATA"); strict decode refuses unknown fields and trailing data ("TRAILING_JSON").
Slot roots and profiles on filesystems with statfs magic 0x01021997, 0x53464846, 0x65735546 or 0x01021994 are refused with "UNQUALIFIED_FILESYSTEM".

Guards are exclusive non-blocking flocks with O_CLOEXEC so helpers cannot keep custody; a held guard returns "SLOT_BUSY: <path>: <errno>" immediately, a non-0600 guard "UNSAFE_GUARD", and an invalid slot id "INVALID_SLOT_ID" (pattern ^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]{1,39}$).

custody refuses "IDENTITY_PROTECTED" (prefixes mv-, srf-id-cuentas-, srf-id-perplexity-, srf-pg-, names srf-egress-proxy, n8n, distil-box, or the live profile), "CREDENTIAL_COPY_CONFIRMATION_REQUIRED" (HumanConfirmed false), "COMPATIBILITY_REQUIRED" (kind not browser/program, or no architecture/image), "FOREIGN_IDENTITY", "IDENTITY_BOUND" (lock file active or unreadable), "UNSAFE_PROFILE" (not 0700 owned by uid 10001), plus CheckStopped errors.

Every Save, Load, Delete, Select and InspectReference first requires that no intent.json exists in the slot; a leftover intent from an interrupted operation (or a failed intent write) returns "SLOT_RECONCILIATION_REQUIRED" until Reconcile runs.

Any unverifiable reference quarantines the whole slot: "SLOT_QUARANTINED: <ref> unverifiable (<reason>); explicitly inspect <other> with InspectReference" with reasons unsafe reference, digest or format invalid, payload verification failed, conflicting generation. A newer format returns "SLOT_FUTURE_VERSION: update required". The highest fully verified generation wins; none gives os.ErrNotExist.

Save refusals before any write: "SLOT_RECONCILIATION_REQUIRED" (intent.json left by an interrupted operation), "SLOT_EXISTS" (CreateOnly), "SLOT_NOT_FOUND" (OverwriteOnly), "FOREIGN_SLOT" (slot owned by another profile), "SLOT_GENERATION_EXHAUSTED", "UNSAFE_SLOT" (symlink in slot), "SLOT_QUOTA" (used bytes including retained generations > MaxBytes-65536), "SLOT_DISK_SPACE".

Save writes intent, packs the profile into a staging dir via the helper, writes manifest.json, renames staging to generations/<manifest sha256>, then publishes a self-hashed reference into A.json (odd generation) or B.json (even), fsyncing at each step, prunes unreferenced generations and clears the intent. Context cancellation after packing but before publication stops without publishing.

Load refusals: "FOREIGN_SLOT" (SourceProfileID mismatch), "SLOT_INCOMPATIBLE: update required" (kind, architecture or image differ), "SLOT_DISK_INODES", "SLOT_DISK_SPACE", "RENAME_EXCHANGE_UNSUPPORTED" (renameat2 exchange probe failed). The slot is unpacked into .slot-load-<slot>.* and atomically exchanged with the profile; the old profile is discarded only after the exchange is durable.

Reconcile replays an interrupted intent under both guards: save prunes and removes staging-*/ref-* leftovers; load proves the exchange outcome from the recorded before/prepared inodes and never retries it ("SLOT_QUARANTINED" when the witnesses do not match); delete resumes finishDelete. ReconcileAll runs it for every slot and refuses "UNSAFE_SLOT" for unexpected entries.

Helper operations run as docker run --rm --pull=never --network none --read-only --cap-drop=ALL plus DAC_OVERRIDE, CHOWN, FOWNER, no-new-privileges, user 0, python3 helperScript. A failed run returns "SLOT_HELPER_REFUSED (<op>)", or "SLOT_HELPER_CLEANUP_UNCERTAIN (<name>)" if docker rm -f also fails (15s); helper output over 4096 bytes is "HELPER_OUTPUT_LIMIT".

The helper refuses links, special files, setuid/setgid/sticky bits, non-10001 ownership, unsafe or duplicate tar member names, more than 100000 entries, paths over 4096 bytes and totals over the cap; SingletonLock, SingletonCookie and SingletonSocket are excluded from packing.

List returns metadata only (slot_id, name, saved_at, generation, size_bytes) for slots of one profile, serialized by listMu so concurrent listings do not refuse each other as SLOT_BUSY; more than 256 entries gives "SLOT_LIST_LIMIT", and any quarantined slot fails the whole listing.

Delete checks custody and ownership ("FOREIGN_SLOT"), writes a delete intent, then removes slot entries, all generations and only this slot's .slot-load-<id>.* stages, keeping the guard and intent until everything is durably removed, so an interrupted delete resumes and never resurrects data.

Provision creates an empty profile directory through the helper after native identity creation; it refuses "IDENTITY_PROTECTED", "UNSAFE_PROFILE" (not a plain directory) and "PROFILE_ALREADY_BOUND" (non-empty), and never overwrites data.

Package cli defines the Runner interface for native CLI execution and the typed Fault{Code, Detail} whose Error() is "<code>: <detail>". Fault is the error type the whole daemon adapter uses for typed refusals; capsule.WireCode turns a Fault code into the wire code seen by core/UI.

ParseLine accepts exactly one bounded closed JSON object line: at most maxBytes, a single optional trailing newline, must start with '{', pass ipc.ValidateJSON limits (MaxDepth 32, MaxStringBytes 65536, MaxKeys 256, MaxArrayItems 4096 [CITED: daemon-adapter/internal/cli/runner.go]) and decode with DisallowUnknownFields. Any violation returns Fault code "malformed_cli" with detail "CLI output is not a bounded closed JSON object"; it is also reused to parse wire params (role switch, record_start, frame_subscribe).
