Maps a native CLI non-zero exit to a Fault code: unknown family -> "unknown_family"; negative exit (killed by signal) -> "uncertain" ("native killed by signal, effect unverified"); srf-host-window -> "host_window_unavailable"; srf-identity-surface and srf-holdings-capsule map exit 2..7 to "usage", "setup", "unavailable", "malformed", "refused", "cli_failed" and any other code to "invalid_exit"; srfd -> "cli_failed". Inferred from capsule.WireCode: lowercase codes reach the wire as ADAPTER_<UPPER> (e.g. ADAPTER_SETUP), except host_window_unavailable which becomes HOST_WINDOW_UNAVAILABLE.

Unsupported(op) returns Fault code "unsupported" with detail "<op> is not configured"; used by Run's stub refusal and by the record path when no recording authority exists (wire code ADAPTER_UNSUPPORTED via wireFailure).

clientAuthority is the ipc authority used by the client runtimes: peer admission, optional core hello revision pin, sender binding to the registered session, and a durable fsynced replay ledger of (sender, seq, nonce) for both inbound and outbound messages.

The ledger is opened O_APPEND|O_NOFOLLOW 0600 and flocked LOCK_EX|LOCK_NB, so a second daemon on the same state dir fails at startup (EWOULDBLOCK). It must be uid-owned, single link, mode 0600 and at most 32 MiB ("private bounded replay ledger required"); each line must parse and pass replay checks, and a last byte other than newline gives "incomplete replay ledger". Any failure is a startup configuration fault.

"replay or capacity refused" when the ledger already holds 100000 entries, seq is 0 or not greater than the last seq for that sender, the nonce is empty, or the nonce was already used; Inferred: after 100000 total entries every further message is refused until the ledger is rotated.

Refusals: "peer refused" (peer uid not current uid); with MV_EXPECTED_CORE_COMMIT set, the first message and any later hello must be hello/v0.2 from core with component_commit equal to the pin, else "core hello revision pin refused"; any envelope whose session_id/from/to differ from the bound registration gives "sender binding refused". Each closes the session.

Reserve appends and fsyncs before admitting; refusals "replay rollback unverified" (a previous failed append could not be truncated and synced, which disables the authority permanently) and "replay byte capacity refused" (ledger would exceed 32 MiB). Failed writes truncate back to the prior size.

Outbound envelopes get seq = last seq for the daemon sender + 1, a random 16-byte hex nonce, msg_id "daemon-<nonce>", ts_ns relative to origin, swapped endpoints and are reserved in the ledger; a clock before origin gives "monotonic origin refused".

NewHandler is the configured dispatch seam for one manager and publisher: it ignores hello/v0.2 (returns nothing), routes capsule_state_request/v0.2 to dispatchState and metaviewer.role_switch/v0.3 to dispatchRoleSwitch, otherwise calls manager.Handle; list results are rewritten by listSnapshots. Nil inputs give "configured manager and publisher required"; a create returning other than one event gives "create must return one surface".

After a non-human create, the initial capture is published and a frame_ready appended. If capture, re-marshal or publish fails, compensate destroys the new surface under a 30 s context detached from cancellation and returns CreationError "initial frame for <id>: <cause>; compensation: <rollback>" with the committed surface_id; human-role openings return created without any frame.

list replies are converted from created to state_changed snapshots; error events pass through; any other schema/event, unknown data fields or empty surface_id fail the whole list with "invalid list snapshot" (a handler error).

capsule_state_request/v0.2 is accepted only from component core ("core state authority required"); on a streaming session it runs in a goroutine with a 3 minute timeout and emits the result asynchronously so state I/O never occupies the data lane.

MV_SRF_NET_MODES, when present, must be a JSON array of unique values from legacy/open/proxied; otherwise startup fails with "MV_SRF_NET_MODES must be a JSON array of network modes" or "invalid MV_SRF_NET_MODES mode". Absent means nil (legacy knowledge).

Mode selection: MV_REWIND_ENABLED must be empty or "1"; rewind conflicts with MV_GUEST_COMMAND_ONLY/MV_HEADLESS_ONLY; MV_REWIND_ONLY=1 needs MV_REWIND_ENABLED=1 and no other mode ("exclusive rewind opt-in required"); MV_GUEST_COMMAND_ONLY must be "1" and exclusive; MV_HEADLESS_ONLY must be "1". Each exclusive mode builds a runtime with no graphical manager. All refusals are Fault code "configuration" printed at startup with exit 2.

Graphical mode requires MV_SRF_BIN_DIR, MV_SRF_STATE_DIR, SRF_IDENTITY_STORE_ROOT, SRF_PROXY_REGISTRY and XDG_RUNTIME_DIR to be absolute ("<KEY> must be absolute"), MV_SESSION_ID/MV_CORE_INSTANCE/MV_DAEMON_INSTANCE non-empty ("<KEY> is required for core registration"), MV_EXPECTED_CORE_COMMIT empty or 40 lowercase hex ("valid expected core revision required"), and MV_SRF_STATE_DIR a canonical no-symlink directory of mode exactly 0700 owned by the current uid ("private canonical state directory required: ...", "private state directory required", "state directory owner refused").

Profiles come from MV_SRF_PROFILES (JSON map, "invalid MV_SRF_PROFILES") or else from MV_SRF_LIVE_PROFILE + MV_SRF_LIVE_RAM_ROOT ("profile map or live profile/root required") with MV_SRF_LIVE_TEXT_INPUT validated ("invalid MV_SRF_LIVE_TEXT_INPUT"); the live fallback is a single browser profile on display :100 at 1280x900 [CITED: daemon-adapter/internal/daemon/environment.go]. Profile RAM roots are then checked by validateProfileRoots.

The capsule manager is built with MaxSurfaces 16, MaxOutputBytes 1<<20 and a 90 s native timeout; one frames.Publisher per distinct profile RAM root shares a single 512 MiB global budget, with MaxFrameBytes 64 MiB, MaxSurfaceBytes 128 MiB, MaxRetained 64 generations and MinRetention 4 s [TARGET]. Failures report "frame budget: ..." or "frame root: ..." as configuration faults at startup.

Transport config: client socket $XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/metaviewer/core.sock, peer uid = current uid, MaxFrameBytes 1 MiB, MaxReplayEntries 100000, MaxConnections 1, HelloTimeout 5 s, ReadTimeout 30 s, WriteTimeout 30 s, ProbeTimeout 1 s, ShutdownTimeout 5 s [CITED: daemon-adapter/internal/daemon/environment.go]. The replay ledger is wire-replay.jsonl opened through /proc/self/fd/<statefd> inside MV_SRF_STATE_DIR; ledger errors become configuration faults.

Schemas load from MV_CONTRACT_DIR (default relative contracts/v0.2). The daemon hello (component daemon, component_version 0.1.1, component_commit from MV_COMPONENT_COMMIT or Go vcs.revision) is validated through the full envelope policy before the socket opens; failure is "configuration: valid build revision required: ...", so a binary built without VCS metadata and without MV_COMPONENT_COMMIT may refuse startup.

Top-level graphical handler routes by body schema: hello/v0.2 -> helloState.accept (builds a fresh manager per session); guest_command_request/v0.2 and rewind_request/v0.2 -> routeGuestCommand; headless_request/v0.2 -> headless manager with each reply validated as an envelope; everything else -> the session handler (subscriptions -> admission -> wire handler).

Each active recording gets one polling goroutine bound to the session context; it TryLocks the per-surface lock every 1 ms until free, polls the recorder, emits events, and exits on a record.Refusal or "recorder is closed". Stop paths cancel and wait for the goroutine (stopRecording, stopSurface on unregister, stopAll on close).

record_request/v0.2 without a recorder: if request_id, surface_id and recording_id (or capture_id) are present, replies record_event/v0.2 event "refused" with reason_code "POLICY" and detail "unsupported: recording authority is not configured"; otherwise a surface_event error with code ADAPTER_UNSUPPORTED.

surface_request record_start/record_stop is translated into record_request ram_start/ram_stop using the recorder's default ring bytes and max fps; missing surface_id or recording_id (or params failing ParseLine) yields a surface_event error with Fault code "usage" (wire ADAPTER_USAGE) and detail "surface_id and recording_id required".

When an input with a proposal_id fails and a previous wire-published frame exists, the reply is not a surface error but an action_receipt/v0.2 with verified=false, after_frame = last published frame (diagnostic only) and error "input failed: <cause>"; without proposal or baseline the failure becomes a surface_event error via wireFailure.

Agent-origin click/type/key input first snapshots the publisher's current frame as baseline; a missing publisher gives "configuration: current input frame publisher required" and no published frame gives "configuration: current published input frame required" (wire ADAPTER_CONFIGURATION, or a verified=false receipt when a proposal and baseline exist).

Destroy releases recorder registration then the owned frame publisher; if either fails the successful destroy events are parked in pendingRelease and the error is returned. A later destroy that gets Fault code "surface" (already gone) replays the parked events, so a retried destroy completes instead of reporting ADAPTER_SURFACE. Release also removes Holdings state sidecars and lastFrames.

On input refused with Fault code SURFACE_NOT_AGENT_CONTROLLED the wire owner calls m.DrainInput for the surface/proposal so a cancelled native completion is acknowledged; the refusal itself passes through unchanged as wire code SURFACE_NOT_AGENT_CONTROLLED.

For non-input ops, replies are emitted before frames: each state_changed with state active and control agent triggers captureStateFrame and an appended frame_ready. Capture failure only logs "adapter: state refresh <id>: <err>; state change remains successful" to stderr; the state change still succeeds.

Input execution time is adapter-observed monotonic completion minus origin; if the clock is below origin or native InputTSNS exceeds completion the input fails with "configuration: monotonic completion refused".

Human-origin input settles immediately without post-input capture: the receipt is action_receipt/v0.2 verified=false with the latest frame and detail "human-origin input; post-input pixel capture skipped". With no baseline at all it synthesises a diagnostic frame_ref (generation 1, ram path /dev/shm/unverified, all-zero sha256) and error "input failed: configuration: post-input frame baseline required". GroundTruth is stripped from native_evidence.

Agent input then captures (with settleInput for type/key and for non-Holdings clicks); refusals: "configuration: post-input capture evidence refused" when evidence.SurfaceID differs or capture predates input, and "configuration: post-input frame publisher required" when no publisher; the capture is published with PublishForced.

observation/v0.2 events (before and after) are emitted only when both GroundTruth values validate, the binding is unchanged (same container, run ID, agent control), both RAMWS files are regular with size W*H*3, generations increase, sidecars write, and the surface is still owned. Otherwise only frame_ready and an action_receipt with verified=false and detail "post-input capture only; expectation verification belongs to core" are sent; the adapter never claims verified=true.

At most 16 Holdings state sidecars (maxRetainedStateSidecars) are retained per surface; the oldest is deleted from disk when the list overflows. Sidecars are named .state-<ramws basename> in the profile RAM root, written O_EXCL|O_NOFOLLOW mode 0600 (writeHoldingsStateSidecar).

wireFailure converts any error into a correlated surface_event/v0.2 event "error" with surface_id (from params, CreationError, or else the envelope msg_id), code = capsule.WireCode(err) and detail = err.Error(). Uppercase Fault codes pass through verbatim (e.g. RAM_ADMISSION_REFUSED, POLICY); non-Fault errors become ADAPTER_ERROR; lowercase codes become ADAPTER_<UPPER>. This is what core/UI sees.
Post-input settle polls every 50 ms within max(1.5 s, 4*first capture cost + 150 ms), capped at a 6 s hard ceiling [TARGET]; non-positive cost gives 1.5 s.

settleInput returns the first capture whose RGB24 hash differs from the baseline, or the last capture when the budget expires; with an empty baseline it returns the first capture. It never invents a change; a later capture timing out returns the last good frame only if the caller's ctx is still live.

MV_SRF_PROFILES is capped at 1 MiB ("profile map byte capacity refused"), bounded by ValidateJSON, decoded with unknown fields refused, and every profile's text_input must be valid ("invalid profile text_input"); RuntimeFromEnv reports any of these as "invalid MV_SRF_PROFILES".

openStateDir requires an absolute clean path and walks it from / one component at a time with O_DIRECTORY|O_NOFOLLOW, holding each descriptor; a symlink anywhere fails. Only a missing final component is created with mode 0700; a missing parent fails with ENOENT.

Shutdown budgets [TARGET]: closeManagerBudget 30 s for list plus every verified destroy, createQuitGrace 10 s, shutdownBudgetCeiling 40 s inside the host's 45 s SIGKILL grace; each destroy gets an equal share of the remaining budget but at least min(remaining, 10 s).

On shutdown every listed surface is destroyed through the same admission handler; when budget is spent the remaining surfaces are not stopped and each adds "shutdown budget exhausted before stopping <id>". All errors are joined and printed to stderr by cleanup; Inferred: those capsules and their RAM reservations then remain on the host.

A second core hello on the same session is refused with Fault "handshake: hello already accepted"; a zero monotonic clock gives "CLOCK_MONOTONIC unavailable"; accept without a stream session gives "session emission required". These are handler errors, so the streaming client tears down the session.

Per session: MV_RING_FPS (integer, default 60) and MV_CAPTURE_RING=1 choose the capture source; one Subscriptions per RAM root with MaxSubscriptions 16, 90 s capture timeout, 5 s shutdown timeout, unchanged-frame dedup and 2 initial unchanged polls. Setup is staged and rolled back so a failed hello leaves no live state.

DISPLAY tap admission uses MV_RAM_ADMISSION_DIR (default $XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/metaviewer/ram-admission), requires uid-owned 0700 ("private RAM admission directory required") and runs checkRAM against the number of reservation entries. It takes the flock non-blocking and proceeds without it if busy, so DISPLAY never waits behind a native create.

Bootstrap for MV_GUEST_COMMAND_ONLY=1 or MV_REWIND_ONLY=1: never builds a graphical manager; requires MV_SESSION_ID/MV_CORE_INSTANCE/MV_DAEMON_INSTANCE, absolute XDG_RUNTIME_DIR, an optional valid core pin, and an owner with a state root ("guest-command-only requires a valid host profile"). Its replay ledger is guest-command-wire-replay.jsonl in the owner's state root.

In guest-command-only mode a failed owner.Close prints "adapter: headless cleanup remains uncertain" (the headless wording), so that stderr line does not by itself identify which runtime failed cleanup.

Handler: repeat hello -> "hello already accepted", request before hello -> "guest-command hello required" (both handler errors that end the session); surface list returns empty; record_request with ids returns record_event refused POLICY "guest-command-only runtime has no recording authority"; any other request returns surface_event error code POLICY "graphical authority is disabled in guest-command-only runtime".

Bootstrap for MV_HEADLESS_ONLY=1: no graphical manager, same registration/XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/pin checks, owner must have a state root ("headless-only requires a valid host profile"), replay ledger headless-wire-replay.jsonl in the protected profile state root.

Handler: repeat hello -> "hello already accepted", request before hello -> "headless hello required"; headless_request/v0.2 goes to the owner with replies envelope-validated; surface list returns empty; record_request refused POLICY "headless-only runtime has no recording authority"; any other request -> surface_event error code POLICY "graphical authority is disabled in headless-only runtime".

In graphical mode a guest-command owner is added only when MV_REWIND_ENABLED=1 (rewind owner plus resource inventory) or MV_ARM64_CAPSULES=1 on GOARCH arm64; MV_ARM64_CAPSULES with another value or on non-arm64 refuses startup "configuration: ARM64 capsule setup mode refused"; other refusals are "guest command profile: ..." and "ARM64 capsule setup requires guest command profile".

guest_command_request/rewind_request without a configured owner returns the handler error "guest command profile unavailable" and without a stream session "guest command streaming session required"; Inferred from stream.go dispatch: either error closes the core session rather than replying.
A nil *resourceinventory.Graphical must be passed to capsule.Config as a nil interface, not a typed-nil interface, otherwise inventory hooks would be enabled on unchanged legacy managers.

Host RAM admission: native creates and destroys are serialized on the core connection and across daemon processes by an flock on a shared directory; MemAvailable is checked before create and after the initial capture. Floor min(20 GiB, MemTotal/4) and 512 MiB reserve per incumbent [TARGET]; a failed post-check compensates only the new surface.

checkRAM refuses with Fault code RAM_ADMISSION_REFUSED, detail "host MemAvailable below floor plus incumbent reserves, or unreadable", when MemAvailable kB < min(20*1024*1024 kB, MemTotal/4) + 512*1024 kB * live, where live is the number of reservation files in the admission directory, or when meminfo is unreadable or inconsistent [TARGET]. The UI receives surface_event error code RAM_ADMISSION_REFUSED.

/proc/meminfo must contain exactly one MemTotal: and one MemAvailable: line, each "<n> kB"; duplicates or bad units give "invalid <field>", and missing fields, total 0 or available > total give "missing or inconsistent host memory". There is no environment override for memory accounting (admissionMemory is a test seam only).

Every profile RAMRoot must be absolute, already clean, existing and equal to its symlink-resolved path ("canonical existing profile RAM root required"), and roots must not nest ("disjoint profile RAM roots required"); both are startup configuration faults.

Only surface_request create and destroy pass through admission; they hold an in-process mutex plus an exclusive (blocking) flock on the admission directory, and records for this owner ("<pid>-<random hex>") are reconciled to the manager's AdmissionProfiles before and after. Owner token or directory failures are wrapped by admissionFault as RAM_ADMISSION_REFUSED "shared RAM admission: <err>".

For create: live = all entries in the directory (including other owners'), checkRAM runs before spawn, then the new profile's reservation file is written and fsynced before the native create so a crash still leaves a conservative record. The create runs under graceContext with createQuitGrace (10 s [TARGET]) so a session quit does not SIGKILL an in-flight start.

After a successful create, checkRAM runs again with the same pre-create live count. On refusal the new surface is destroyed under a 30 s context detached from cancellation; if removal is verified (state_changed destroyed) the UI sees RAM_ADMISSION_REFUSED for that surface, otherwise a CreationError carrying the surface_id, cause and rollback error is returned (code still RAM_ADMISSION_REFUSED via errors.As).

graceContext detaches from the parent's cancellation and cancels only grace after the parent is cancelled, preserving parent values; createGrace=0 (test seam) reproduces the old behaviour where a cancelled session kills the in-flight create.

A pre-create RAM refusal detail adds "(reservation records counted: N" and, when other owners' records exist, ", of which M belong to other owners ... inspect with `python3 tools/mv_ram_admission.py reclaim --dry-run`, apply only after the dry run proves the native containers absent)". PID death never reclaims records, so stale records from a crashed daemon keep refusing creates until reclaimed.

Admission directory is MV_RAM_ADMISSION_DIR or $XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/metaviewer/ram-admission (parent created via openStateDir); errors "absolute XDG_RUNTIME_DIR required" and "uid-owned 0700 admission directory required", then a blocking LOCK_EX flock. All daemons of a uid must share this path; each error reaches the UI as RAM_ADMISSION_REFUSED "shared RAM admission: ...".

Reservation files are named <owner>-<sha256(profile) hex>--<profile>, created O_NOFOLLOW mode 0600 and fsynced; profile IDs must match ^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]{0,63}$ or sync fails with "invalid reservation profile" (RAM_ADMISSION_REFUSED). Only this owner's unwanted files are removed; other owners' files are never touched.

metaviewer.role_switch/v0.3 must come from component core ("core role authority required"), parse as a bounded closed object, and have request_id and surface_id matching ^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._:-]{0,127}$ and role human or agent ("invalid role switch"). These are handler errors, so they close the session.

A role switch replies metaviewer.role_switch_result/v0.3 {request_id, surface_id, role, ok}; on SwitchRole failure it adds code = capsule.WireCode(err) and sends no state_changed; on success it sends state_changed then the ok result.

Commands declares internal routing for 14 surface ops (create, list, destroy, take_control, release_control, input, frame_subscribe, frame_unsubscribe, view, login, view-stop, record_start, record_stop, screenshot) through a capsule.New(nil, nil) backend; the comment states it grants no wire authority and every route shares the backend's configuration refusal.

Run is the startup gate. It returns 2 with stderr "adapter: unsupported arguments" for any CLI argument, "adapter: startup cancelled" if ctx is already done, "adapter: one runtime required" for more than one Runtime, and "adapter: policy and handler required" when Policy or Handler is nil. A client runtime dials core (connectStreaming when Streaming), otherwise it listens with ipc.Listen/ipc.Serve; any transport error is printed and returns 2, clean finish returns 0. Close runs on every exit via defer.

With no Runtime supplied, Run refuses startup with "unsupported: authority policy: authenticated sender binding, durable replay and outbound identity is not configured" and exit 2; Commands() is only built, it grants no wire authority.

Forces a fresh published frame after a successful active agent state update; refuses "state refresh requires agent control" for human role or non-agent control and "state refresh publisher required" when no publisher, failures being diagnostic only for state changes.

The production transport: the daemon dials core's Unix socket (dial timeout = HelloTimeout) rather than listening. It refuses with "complete client registration required" unless registration is core->daemon with a session ID, "unix peer required" for non-Unix conns, and "core peer credentials refused" when SO_PEERCRED uid does not match; all end Run with exit 2.

Every outbound message is wrapped by policy.Wrap under a lock, re-validated against the contract ("outbound contract: ...") and framed. On connect the local hello is passed to the handler and then the daemon hello is written first, within HelloTimeout (5 s [CITED: daemon-adapter/internal/daemon/environment.go]). An emit failure cancels the whole session.

Message IDs of outbound frame_ref/frame_ready are retained for STALE_FRAME verdict correlation, bounded to cfg.MaxReplayEntries (100000 in the env runtime [CITED: daemon-adapter/internal/daemon/environment.go]) with oldest eviction.

Any error returned by the handler (not a reply event) fails the whole session with "dispatch: <err>" and cancels it. So handler errors such as "invalid role switch", "core state authority required", "guest command profile unavailable" or "invalid list snapshot" drop the core connection instead of producing a correlated refusal.

The data worker serializes requests per surface_id lock (or the shared work lock when no surface_id); frame_subscribe, frame_unsubscribe and destroy run without the surface lock so a drain is not blocked by an in-flight capture holding it.

Inbound validation closes the session on: envelope policy failure; envelope schema not matching body, endpoints or session_id differing from registration, seq 0 or empty nonce ("registered core route refused"); capsule_envelope/rewind_envelope before core hello ("authenticated core hello required before requests"); or a body schema outside the allowed list ("core surface request required").

Each inbound envelope is authenticated and its seq/nonce durably reserved before dispatch; failure ends the session. Consumed without dispatch: the first core hello, action_verdict refused POLICY (logged "daemon: consumed policy refusal proposal_id=..."), and action_verdict refused STALE_FRAME only when the proposal_id matches a frame message ID this daemon sent.

Core keepalive probes are answered in the reader before any queue. take_control, release_control and role switches go to the control lane (capacity 64) and become a gate: data queued after them waits for completion. Data goes through an unbounded-to-256 FIFO staging buffer (maxDataBacklog 256, dataCh 64) so control frames are not head-of-line blocked.

Handles frame_subscribe/frame_unsubscribe and wraps role switches: role switch unsubscribes active subscriptions, runs the switch, then restores only pre-existing subscriptions. Unsubscribe drains every root's subscription before replying (no reply events). Subscribe needs the surface binding and a publisher for its profile root, else surface_event error "configuration: subscription publisher required" (ADAPTER_CONFIGURATION); malformed params give ADAPTER_MALFORMED_CLI.

diagLimiter rate-limits per-surface diagnostics on stderr: skipped-poll counts are aggregated over a 30 s window [CITED: daemon-adapter/internal/frames/diag_limiter.go], MV_ADAPTER_DIAG=verbose restores per-event lines and a 5 s stage_summary cadence.
recordSkippedPolls returns the summed skipped polls once per window when non-zero; in verbose mode or with the limiter disabled it returns every miss immediately.
Error and warning diagnostic lines are never rate-limited unless the faultRateLimitErrors test flag is set.

DisplayTapRefusal carries typed codes DISPLAY_MISSING ("invalid DISPLAY target: missing capsule display"), DISPLAY_INVALID ("invalid DISPLAY target") and DISPLAY_UNSUPPORTED ("DISPLAY requires browser or program window"); it unwraps to a cli.Fault with the same code and leaves VERIFIED capture unaffected.
The DISPLAY ring base is MV_DISPLAY_DIR when set, else /dev/shm/metaviewer-display-<uid>, independent of the app's XDG_RUNTIME_DIR.

DisplayTaps runs one best-effort DISPLAY tap goroutine per surface id that streams window pixels into a per-surface tmpfs ring for the UI; it never calls Capture or the Publisher. Start is a no-op when MV_DISPLAY_TAP=off, the id fails ^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._-]{0,63}$, the taps are closed, or a task already exists.
StartReplies starts a tap for every admitted create reply event: a "created" event with a surface_id, or a "frame_ready" event whose frame_ref generation is > 0.

Restart backoff starts at 100 ms and doubles to a 2 s cap after each ended session [CITED: daemon-adapter/internal/frames/displaytap.go]; a resize (errDisplayResized) resets it to 100 ms and restarts immediately.

If the RAM Admit hook refuses, the tap records the error and exits for good, printing "adapter: DISPLAY tap refused by RAM admission" once; the tile gets no DISPLAY ring until the tap is restarted by a new create/frame_ready reply.

A Resolve error is retried (same backoff) only when it is an errno, io.EOF or io.ErrUnexpectedEOF and not a cli.Fault; any other resolve error or a validDisplayTarget refusal ends the tap and is kept in DisplayTaps.Err(id).

For host windows a session error containing minimized/iconic/unmapped calls OnMinimized(id,true); an error containing host_window_unavailable:, witness, closed, no such window, badwindow, baddrawable, destroyed, not found or gone calls OnTerminal with the extracted reason and stops the tap (the daemon then emits a lost event).

Host tap terminal/minimized classification is substring matching on error text (including sender stderr), so a stderr message containing words like "gone" or "not found" ends the tap; the default reason is "host_window_unavailable: window closed or witness changed", truncated to 256 bytes.

A DISPLAY target must have a non-empty display (else DISPLAY_MISSING); capsule displays must match ^:[0-9]+$, host windows ^:[0-9]+(\.[0-9]+)?$ plus a non-empty witness and absolute BinDir; container and run must be safe ring components, XID != 0 and width/height in 1..4096, else DISPLAY_INVALID.
Each tap session is capped at 9 minutes (renewed below the recorder session cap) and gets a fresh ring generation of UnixNano + an atomic counter, which makes the UI reopen the ring.

When a decoded frame's size differs from the binding, OnResize (if set) updates geometry and the session restarts via errDisplayResized; with no geometry owner a native tap reopens the ring at the witnessed size. A host-window frame clears the minimized flag via OnMinimized(id,false).
While a session runs, every 250 ms the tap re-resolves the binding; any error or changed target ends the session with "DISPLAY binding retired" and the supervisor restarts with the new binding.

Shutdown is bounded: a STOP control frame gets a 20 ms write deadline, then the sender has 100 ms to exit before the whole process group is SIGKILLed; the ring is unmapped and its file removed afterwards.

Production capsule capture is one resident `docker exec -i -u 10001:10001 -e DISPLAY=:100 <container> sh -c` loop running /usr/local/libexec/srf-fbread getimage :100 <xid> then sleep 0.03 (about 30 fps [CITED: daemon-adapter/internal/frames/displaytap.go]); a failing getimage exits 9. Host windows run <BinDir>/srf-host-window capture --xid <xid> --witness <w> instead.

ResolveDisplayTarget maps host-window/host-xpra bindings directly; other kinds must be browser or program with a window (else DISPLAY_UNSUPPORTED). It reads <stateDir>/<container>.json without following links and refuses "unsafe DISPLAY identity state" (not a regular 0600 file owned by the euid, or > 1 MiB) and "DISPLAY state mismatch" (not ready or container/run_id differ); a window missing from xids yields a strconv parse error.

The W8U framed decoder (used only when a Command seam is set for a non-host target) refuses with "DISPLAY control header", "DISPLAY END length", "DISPLAY HELLO", "DISPLAY framing", "DISPLAY frame header", "DISPLAY leg A length", "DISPLAY leg B length"; it performs no per-frame hash and ACKs each sequence.
XWD leg validation refuses "DISPLAY XWD short" (< 100 bytes) and "DISPLAY XWD geometry" (size/visual/masks 0xff0000/0xff00/0xff/stride mismatch with the target).

The XWD stream decoder ends the session with "DISPLAY XWD header" unless header_size is 100..4096, version 7, format 2 (ZPixmap), byte order <= 1, 32 bpp, 1..4096 per dimension, bytes_per_line in [4w, 4w+64] and ncolors <= 256; it stamps each frame with wall-clock UnixNano as capture_mono.
DisplayRingPath returns <runtimeDir>/metaviewer/display/<surface_id>.ring; an unsafe surface id is refused with DISPLAY_INVALID "invalid DISPLAY surface id".

The ring directory must be tmpfs (0x01021994), owned by the euid and mode 0700, else "DISPLAY requires private tmpfs directory ..."; the file is 0600, size 64 + 2*w*h*3, header MVDISP1, width@8, height@12, stride@16, format 1@20, seq@24 (starts 1), capture_mono@32, generation@40 (little-endian).
A leftover ring file is reclaimed only if it is a regular 0600 single-link tmpfs file owned by the euid; otherwise open fails with "unsafe stale DISPLAY ring" and the tap session ends.

publish is a seqlock writer: seq is set odd, the RGB24 frame is copied into slot (next/2)%2, capture_mono written, then seq set to the next even value. It refuses "DISPLAY RGB length" and "DISPLAY ring geometry changed".
close unmaps and removes the ring file, so a reader sees the ring absent between tap sessions (Inferred: the tile shows its absent/stale DISPLAY state until the next session publishes).

Ref is the frame_ref wire object (schema, surface_id, generation, tick, ts_ns, width, height, format, ramws_path, sha256, capture_us) that the Publisher mints and Subscriptions sends to the UI inside frame_ready events.

The default frames Backend from New() refuses both operations with cli.Unsupported, i.e. code "unsupported" with detail "frame_subscribe is not configured" / "frame_unsubscribe is not configured"; real capture goes through Subscriptions instead.

Publisher turns a verified native frame (PNG, .rgb24 file or ring payload) into an immutable adapter-owned .rgb file in a private frames-* directory under the RAM root and mints a frame_ref generation; it keeps a time- and byte-bounded ring of recent publications per surface.

Retention bounds: 64 MiB small-budget surface cap, 128 MiB live surface cap, 256 MiB max surface, 512 MiB default total, 1024 MiB max total, 4 s live min retention, 60 s max retention [CITED: daemon-adapter/internal/frames/publisher.go]. The daemon configures MaxFrameBytes 64 MiB, MaxSurfaces 16, MaxRetained 64, MinRetention 4 s, a shared 512 MiB Budget [CITED: daemon-adapter/internal/daemon/environment.go].
Almost every Publisher refusal is the single untyped error "frame identity, allocation or pixels refused"; Subscriptions turns it into a capture_failed event, so the UI cannot see which check failed.

NewPublisher refuses (frameError) out-of-range budgets or a RAMRoot that is not a clean path under /dev/shm/; openRAMRoot refuses a non-tmpfs, world-writable or foreign-owned root and requires the frames-* output dir to be 0700.

Source frames are opened component-by-component with O_NOFOLLOW under the binding's frames root and must be a tmpfs regular file owned by the euid, no group/other bits, one link, 1..MaxFrameBytes bytes, and unchanged (fstat before == after except atime); otherwise frameError.

PNG frames must match the IHDR width/height, decode to the same bounds, be fully opaque (alpha 255 in extractRGB24/compactRGBA8ToRGB24), and their RGB24 SHA-256 must equal the native sha256_rgb24; else frameError.
Any failed publish attempt clears skipReady, disabling the digest skip until another verified publication.

publish refuses (frameError) a closed publisher, id not equal to the binding surface id, container != native generation, seq 0 or not increasing, malformed sha256, too many surfaces, frame larger than the surface geometry or pixel/byte budgets, or a window id/size mismatch.

Digest skip: when dedup is requested, the refresh epoch matches, skipReady is true and the native sha256/size equal the last ref, publish skips source I/O, refreshes the last ref's retention time, returns the old Ref with changed=false and Skipped=1; no frame_ready is sent, so the tile keeps showing the last frame.

Before writing, publish plans evictions: oldest refs beyond MaxRetained, beyond the per-surface byte cap, or older than MinRetention go first, never below 2 per surface; then the global total cap evicts the oldest ref across all publishers sharing the Budget. If it still does not fit, frameError.
publish refuses (frameError) if the output directory path no longer resolves to the held directory before or after linking, so a replaced frames-* directory stops all publication for that publisher.
A successful publish increments the publisher-wide generation and returns Ref{schema "frame_ref/v0.2", format "rgb24", ramws_path <frames dir>/<32 hex>.rgb, tick = native seq} with changed=true.

Release unlinks all owned .rgb leases for a surface (ENOENT tolerated), records each unlink immediately, runs release hooks (which clear Subscriptions confirmation and failures) and returns frameError for an unknown surface or closed publisher.
Close unlinks every retained lease, keeps failures for retry, removes the frames-* directory and detaches from the shared Budget; source PNGs are never removed.

Current returns a copy of the latest published Ref without capturing; nil/closed publisher, unknown surface, no refs, or a ref with wrong id, generation 0 or empty sha256 returns frameError ("frame identity, allocation or pixels refused").

SelectRingSource picks the capture source once per session: legacy pair capture at 100 ms per poll by default; with MV_CAPTURE_RING=1 and a validated ring root it uses RingSource and RingPollInterval(fps). When enabled it prints capture_mode=<mode> reason="..." to the report writer; a refused root keeps legacy mode with the refusal as reason.

RingSource is the opt-in (MV_CAPTURE_RING=1) resident capture source that reads OpenSuperficies ring files under the compiled root /dev/shm/vqa-ring and hands verified RGB24 payloads (at most two per surface) to the Publisher; failures after selection never fall back to the CLI.

RingError codes: ring_root, ring_wire, ring_missing, ring_hostile, ring_length, ring_geometry, ring_stale, ring_torn (detail "resident ring refused"); ring_stale and ring_torn unwrap to context.DeadlineExceeded so they never count as proven absence.
RingPollInterval clamps fps to 1..120 and caps the poll spacing at 40 ms; the daemon passes MV_RING_FPS or default 60 [CITED: daemon-adapter/internal/daemon/environment.go], giving about 16.7 ms.

NewRingSource refuses ring_root if the vqa-ring group is missing or the root is not tmpfs with nosuid,nodev,noexec, not a directory of mode 02770, or not owned by the euid and vqa-ring gid. Defaults: 4 slot-read retries, 500 ms max frame age.
Per-window directories <root>/<run>/<window> (holdings use the container suffix as window) refuse ring_wire for unsafe names, ring_missing when absent, ring_hostile when not a checked directory.

read requires exactly one regular ring.rgb24 (0640, uid euid or 10001, vqa-ring gid, single link) and an OSRG v1 header (1..16 slots, 1..4096 px, stride w*3, 1..120 fps); it refuses ring_hostile, ring_length, ring_wire, ring_geometry (larger than the surface, or geometry changed from the pinned value). If no slot is stable and SHA-256-valid it returns ring_stale when a frame was older than maxAge, else ring_torn.

host-window, host-xpra and vm bindings always use Manager.Capture (native pair). For resident captures, any RingError other than ring_missing/ring_stale/ring_torn forgets the surface state and stops the resident writer via RefuseResident; the error is returned, wrapped with "writer stop:" if stopping fails.
take hands the stored payload to the Publisher only for an exact Path/Seq/Generation/SHA match; otherwise ring_wire.

Subscriptions owns per-surface capture polling: a 2-stage pipeline (capture N+1 overlaps publish/emit of N) paced by a monotonic clock independently of UI visibility, emitting frame_ready events to the UI and rate-limited stage diagnostics.
Per-surface stage_summary lines (capture/decode/hash/write/total p50 and p95 in ms) are printed once per diagnostics window, default 30 s, with at most 4096 samples kept.

NewSubscriptions refuses "complete bounded subscription dependencies required" when MaxSubscriptions < 1, a non-positive interval/timeout, negative InitialUnchangedPolls or a nil source/publisher/emit.

Subscribe refuses "inactive session or invalid surface identity" (closed session, empty or > 128-byte id), "surface subscription is stopping" (task cancelled but not drained) and "subscription capacity reached" (MaxSubscriptions, 16 in the daemon [CITED: daemon-adapter/internal/daemon/environment.go]). Re-subscribing a live surface keeps the poller and resets confirmation so the next capture is published even if unchanged.

Capture waits for the per-surface lock by TryLock polling every 1 ms until the capture timeout (90 s in the daemon [CITED: daemon-adapter/internal/daemon/environment.go]); a long-held surface lock therefore delays that tile without failing it.

native_busy faults, host-window resize and host-window waiting are transient and reset failure counts; a binding already in state "lost" marks lost at once; otherwise the first failure is transient and the second consecutive failure terminates, marking lost only if both were absence faults (confirmedLossCaptureFailures = 2).

Missed poll deadlines are counted, never queued: next is advanced to the next interval boundary after now and the misses are recorded as skipped_polls ("adapter: surface <id> skipped_polls=<n> total_skipped_polls=<n>").

A publish or delivery failure drops that frame, resets confirmation, logs "frame failure (n/2), dropped; retry with next capture" and retries; the 2nd consecutive failure (maxConsecutiveFrameFailures = 2) terminates the subscription.

Dedup is enabled only after the surface has at least InitialUnchangedPolls (default 2) confirmed deliveries and one emitted frame in this task, so the first frames are always published even when pixels are unchanged.
A changed publication is sent as {schema "surface_event/v0.2", event "frame_ready", data.frame_ref}; an unchanged one sends nothing and only records stage durations.

On a confirmed loss the source's BeginMarkLost event (state_changed lost) is emitted first with the capture timeout; if it is not delivered the task ends with the joined error; the capture_failed event follows only after loss delivery is complete.

Terminal capture, publication or delivery failure emits an error event with code "capture_failed" and detail "capture, publication or delivery refused (skipped_polls=<n>)" under schema surface_event/v0.2; this is what the UI sees, the precise cause goes only to stderr ("adapter: surface <id> error: ...").

Unsubscribe cancels and waits for the task to drain up to ShutdownTimeout (5 s in the daemon), returning the context error on timeout; it clears only its own failure record so a replacement keeps its own terminal result.
TerminalError returns the retained error of a finished failed task; at most MaxSubscriptions failures are retained, oldest evicted first (see poll defer).

Manager owns at most one private ARM64 guest-command controller service per daemon session: one create attempt, a pending map of request bodies, a seen-event set, and a reservation marker path. It is built by NewFromEnv and driven by internal/daemon/normal_guest_command.go (Handle) on the authenticated core session.

The public reservation_id is "reservation-" plus SHA-256 over the domain tag MetaViewer/guest-command/reservation/v1\0 and the 4-byte big-endian length-prefixed session ID and request ID. The Python controller computes the same value in guest_command_runtime/protocol.py reservation_id, so both sides must stay byte-identical.

Guest commands are off unless MV_GUEST_COMMAND_PROFILE is set (empty returns nil, nil). Startup fails with "guardian conflict" if MV_GUEST_COMMAND_GUARDIAN_UNIT differs from the profile guardian, with guardian errors from verifyGuardian, or with "previous reservation requires reconciliation" if StateRoot/guest-command-reservation.json already exists; the daemon then has no guest-command owner.

Handle returns a Go error (not a refusal event) for: "complete authenticated guest request required" (bad schema, empty request_id/session, nil validate/emit), "session changed" (a different core session after first create), "guest owner unavailable" (closing), and "guest owner uncertain" (poisoned). While poisoned, only a stop with a bound child and retained session is admitted, via reconcileStop.

Refusal codes emitted as guest_command_event/v0.2 event "refused" with session null: DUPLICATE (request_id already pending), CAPACITY (256 or more pending entries), BUSY (a second create after one attempt), UNAVAILABLE (create while config_template runtime_admitted is not true).

Create poisons the owner if prepare, inventory ServicePending, or the service factory fails; any send failure (3-second deadline) poisons it and returns "guest send uncertain: ...". A poisoned owner never replays; later requests get "guest owner uncertain" except reconciling stop.
A run, cancel or stop before any child exists is refused with code UNAVAILABLE; otherwise the request body is recorded in pending before it is sent.

A single reader goroutine reads service lines with a 180-second per-read timeout and consumes them under the manager mutex. A read error calls failLocked; a consume error poisons and calls failLocked. The reader exits when closing is set or the child has been cleared by a verified stop.

Every service event must pass the schema validator and match guest_command_event/v0.2, the profile owner_id and the reservation token, else "guest event schema" or "guest authority mismatch". Event IDs are single-use with an 8192 cap ("guest event replay/capacity"); events must correlate to a pending request ("uncorrelated guest event"); the first session must come from the create accepted event ("unbound guest"), and workload/generation may never change ("guest identity changed"). The first binding is durably written to <marker>.bound.

Allowed event order per request: accepted once with matching op; output only for an accepted run; ready only for an accepted create; job_finished only for an accepted run; refused only before acceptance ("refusal after effect"); outcome_unknown marks all pending done; stopped requires accepted stop, native_absent true, phase stopped and ownership released, then closes the child and writes <marker>.closed. Any other kind is "unknown event". Accepted events are then forwarded via emit.

When the service transport dies, one synthetic outcome_unknown event with data.code TRANSPORT is emitted for the active request (a run is preferred), the session is rewritten to phase uncertain and ownership held, an unfinished run job becomes state unknown with output_complete false, pending cancel/stop controls show ack pending, and the owner is poisoned. The UI sees the capsule as uncertain/held rather than stopped.

Reconciling stop sends no guest command: it requires a new request_id ("stop replay") whose workload_id and generation match the bound guest ("stop target mismatch"), writes <marker>.reconcile, emits accepted, closes the retained service by its retained identity, writes <marker>.closed, and returns a stopped event with native_absent true. Errors "missing uncertain state" and "missing controls" stop it.
Close sets closing, closes the child with a 10-second deadline, waits for the reader, and always seals the inventory (errors joined). A reader still running at the deadline returns the context error.
The host-only inventory binding must be installed before the first create and its Actor must equal the profile owner_id; otherwise "inventory owner binding".

All reservation markers and launch files are created with O_CREAT|O_EXCL mode 0600, fsynced, then the parent directory is fsynced, so an existing marker is never overwritten and a crash leaves durable evidence.

prepare checks StateRoot and RuntimeRoot are private 0700 directories, durably writes the pending reservation marker (schema guest-command-reservation/v1, unit mv-guest-command-<nonce>.service) before any process exists, then builds attempt-*/ with bundle/ files re-pinned by SHA-256 (2 MiB cap each), runner.py (1 MiB cap), a copied pinned python (mode 0500), launch.json, and <marker>.prepared with device/inode identities.

Rewind profiles use the runtime directory prefix "r-" instead of "headless-" because the protected rewind base has a 70-byte native Unix-path limit (comment) [CITED: daemon-adapter/internal/guestcommand/prepare.go].

Service identity is InvocationID (32 hex), MainPID, canonical ControlGroup, the process start time (field 22 of /proc/<pid>/stat) and the cgroup directory device/inode; the main PID must be the only member path 0::<group>. Errors: "active invocation required", "main PID required", "canonical cgroup required", "cgroup identity absent", "process stat malformed", "process start absent", "main cgroup mismatch".

The guardian unit must be active with a non-root ControlGroup ("guardian inactive") and the daemon's own /proc/self/cgroup must be that group or below it ("daemon outside guardian"). Checked at NewFromEnv and again before each service start.

The controller runs via systemd-run --user in newton-ia.slice, BindsTo/After the guardian unit, KillMode=control-group, Restart=no, env -i PATH=/usr/bin:/bin, python -I -B. Rewind profile: MemoryHigh=6G, MemoryMax=8G, MemorySwapMax=0, CPUQuota=200%, TasksMax=256, UMask=0077, no RuntimeMaxSec. Normal guest command: MemoryMax=512M, MemorySwapMax=0, CPUQuota=100%, TasksMax=64, RuntimeMaxSec=180, TimeoutStopSec=5.

Before systemd-run, both the profile python and the copied attempt python must still match the pin and execute an import probe whose sys.prefix and sys.base_prefix equal python_prefix; failures surface as "interpreter import probe failed" or "interpreter prefix mismatch" and poison the owner.

Readiness requires, within 10 seconds, a first line {"guest_command_ready":true,"cgroup":"/sys/fs/cgroup/.../<unit>"} ("service readiness witness"), systemd showing the same active cgroup ("service cgroup mismatch"), a stable pidfd on MainPID ("stable pidfd unavailable"), and an unchanged identity on re-read ("service changed during pidfd acquisition"). Then service.json is written and the inventory ServiceBound is called.
Request lines must be under 262144 bytes ("request line bound"); a write that misses its deadline closes stdin so no partial line can later complete. The stdout scanner buffer is also 262144 bytes.

Close closes stdin, waits up to 2 seconds, then SIGTERMs only through the retained pidfd if the identity is unchanged ("service replaced or unknown; no signal"). Closure is proven only if the unit is inactive/failed with the same invocation and cgroup, the main process is gone, and the cgroup is absent or has "populated 0"; otherwise errors such as "service still active", "replacement service; closure unknown", "owned main process closure unproved", "service cgroup populated". On failure inventory.Unknown is recorded instead of ServiceClosed.

Every pinned source is opened O_NOFOLLOW and refused ("file custody refused") if it is a hard-linked file, group/other-writable, owned by someone other than root or the daemon user, or (for the profile) not 0600-private; any change during the read fails "source changed during read". Editing a pinned file in place without updating its sha256 fails "pin mismatch".

Load (schema mv-guest-command-host/v1, controller guest_command_runtime/controller.py) and LoadRewind (schema mv-rewind-host/v1, controller rewind_runtime/controller.py) read the owner-private host profile (65536-byte cap), reject duplicate keys and unknown fields, and require owner_id actor-<64 hex>, a valid guardian unit name, distinct private StateRoot/RuntimeRoot, a canonical python_prefix, and pinned python and runner. Errors include "profile identity", "distinct roots required", "canonical Python prefix required", "config authority mismatch".

The dependency closure is an exact list of pinned files, not a directory scan: normal profiles need 11 guest_command_runtime modules; rewind profiles need 8 guest_command_runtime modules (without native, storage, controller) plus rewind_runtime __init__, config, native, controller. Any extra or repeated relative path fails "dependency closure" and any missing one fails "missing dependency". No "exhaustive manifest inventory" string is raised here.

Normal config_template: schema guest-command-host-config/v1, explicit runtime_admitted boolean, generation 1..9007199254740991, startup_seconds and stop_seconds 1..30, exactly four artifacts engine, kernel, broker, busybox with absolute clean paths and 64-hex digests; otherwise "config template contract" or "artifact contract".

The ARM64 rewind owner requires MV_REWIND_ENABLED=1 ("rewind opt-in required") and MV_REWIND_PROFILE ("rewind profile required"); MV_REWIND_GUARDIAN_UNIT may not conflict ("rewind guardian conflict"); a leftover StateRoot/rewind-reservation.json refuses start with "prior rewind requires reconciliation". Called from internal/daemon/normal_guest_command.go and environment.go.

Rewind Handle accepts guest_command_request/v0.2 and rewind_request/v0.2. Go errors: "authenticated rewind owner request required", "foreign core session", "owner closing", "owner transport uncertain". Refusals: DUPLICATE (pending request_id), CAPACITY (256 pending, or 255 for anything but a guest stop, which keeps the last slot for cleanup), UNAVAILABLE for every cancel, BUSY while any non-done request exists (stop may overlap non-stop work).

Create is refused BUSY after one attempt and UNAVAILABLE without runtime_admitted; otherwise it sets generation 1, epoch 1, a fresh expected workload-<nonce>, phase initializing, and prepares and starts the service exactly like the normal guest owner.

For non-create requests: UNAVAILABLE without a child; STALE if workload_id/generation (and for rewind, authority_epoch) differ; BUSY unless phase is ready or paused (restore also allowed from recoverable). pause needs ready; resume needs paused; mark and restore and resume bump generation and epoch (mark only when ready); unknown rewind op or unparsable ring is INVALID; overflow past 9007199254740991 is CAPACITY. Guest-family run is BUSY unless phase is ready.

The point ring holds at most two points: with fewer than two no victim is chosen; with exactly two the oldest point with active_references 0 (ties by point_id) is the victim; any other count, or two mapped points, is refused CAPACITY. The new point_id is point-<SHA-256 over length-prefixed session, workload, request_id>.

Each request is sent to the service as a private packet {request, binding, point_id, public_reservation}; binding carries owner_id, workload_id, generation, authority_epoch, session-<sha256(session NUL request_id)> and a per-request reservation_id. A send failure poisons the owner.

Guest-family events from the rewind service must carry the expected workload and current generation ("guest binding drift") and belong to a guest-family request ("cross-family guest event"); they are then checked by Manager.consumeLocked and move phase to ready, stopped or uncertain.

Rewind events must be rewind_event/v0.2, valid, owner-bound, unseen, and correlated ("rewind event authority", "rewind correlation"); the session must keep workload, owner, planned generation and epoch with ownership held ("rewind binding changed"). accepted must show pausing/resuming/marking/restoring; completed must show the planned phase and point; mark must yield exactly prior points minus victim plus new point ("mark ring shape"/"mark ring changed"/"mark point missing"); restore needs last_good_usable equal to the point and only it referenced. Unknown kinds fail "rewind event kind".

Recovery after a failed restore is admitted only when phase is uncertain, the restore is done, data.no_active_vmm is true, failed_request_id is that request, point and last_good_usable match the plan, session phase is recoverable, and no point is still referenced; otherwise "unproven recovery" or "recovery still mapped". Phase then becomes recoverable so only restore is admitted.

On rewind transport loss the owner is poisoned and phase becomes uncertain. Without a rewind session or a pending rewind request it delegates to Manager.failLocked for guest-family requests only (code TRANSPORT); otherwise it emits a rewind_event/v0.2 outcome_unknown with code TRANSPORT, phase uncertain and pending_request_id for each pending rewind request.

Rewind config_template: schema rewind-host-config/v1, explicit runtime_admitted, owner actor-<64 hex>, startup_seconds and stop_seconds 1..10, canonical runtime_root and external_cgroup, and four artifacts whose sha256 must equal fixed reviewed pins (engine fe726e0b..., kernel 43597af5..., broker 0b3a451d..., busybox 52151e7f...). Errors: "rewind template contract", "rewind template paths", "rewind artifact pin".

headless.Manager owns one host-configured persistent headless controller service (mc06-controller) with a synchronous request/response loop. Enabled only by MV_HEADLESS_PROFILE; used by internal/daemon/environment.go and headless_environment.go.

Empty MV_HEADLESS_PROFILE disables headless. Start fails with "guardian conflict" if MV_HEADLESS_GUARDIAN_UNIT conflicts, a guardian error, or "previous reservation requires reconciliation" when StateRoot/headless-reservation.json exists.

Headless refusals are headless_event/v0.2 refused events with data.effect not_dispatched and codes: UNAVAILABLE (nil owner or runtime_admitted not true), OUT_OF_ORDER (after outcome_unknown, anything but stop), DUPLICATE_REQUEST (request_id seen before), BUSY (second create), UNKNOWN_WORKLOAD (non-create with no child). Go errors: "headless request required", "headless responsibility uncertain; no replay" (poisoned), "headless request bound" (128 request IDs).

Each request is sent with a 35-second deadline and expects at most two events: accepted or refused first, then a terminal refused/completed/state_changed/outcome_unknown. Violations poison the owner: "invalid controller event contract", "uncorrelated headless event", "controller event order", "controller owner mismatch", "unbound controller identity", "controller identity changed", "unexpected release", "event sequence", "missing terminal event". A stopped/released session closes the child and writes <marker>.closed.

After a send or read failure the owner is poisoned and, only if a session was previously acknowledged, a synthetic outcome_unknown event with code OUTCOME_UNKNOWN (phase uncertain, ownership held, run job status unknown) is returned; with no session it returns the error "headless unknown without a valid session: ..." so no workload is invented.

Headless service caps: MemoryMax=512M, MemorySwapMax=0, CPUQuota=100%, TasksMax=64, RuntimeMaxSec=180, TimeoutStopSec=5, KillMode=control-group, BindsTo the guardian. Request lines must be under 65536 bytes (Send) and readiness is the line {"mc09_ready":true,...}.

Headless readiness mirrors guestcommand: "service readiness witness" (missing mc09_ready line within 10 s), "service cgroup mismatch", "stable pidfd unavailable", "service changed during pidfd acquisition"; then attempt/service.json is written.

Headless Close uses the same closure proof as guestcommand (2-second grace, pidfd SIGTERM only for an unchanged identity, inactive unit, same invocation/cgroup, process done, cgroup absent or populated 0) but has no inventory hooks.

Headless profile schema mv-headless-host/v1 with controller_relative mc06-controller/controller.py and an exact 8-file closure (mc06-controller controller/arm_backend/contract_guard, mc04-runtime/arm_harness.py, mc05 reference_model and three v0.2 headless schemas); errors "profile identity", "dependency closure", "missing dependency", "config authority mismatch".

Headless config_template: schema mc06-host-config/v1, explicit runtime_admitted, generation 1..9007199254740991, resources mem_size_mib exactly 256 and vcpu_count exactly 1, deadlines startup_seconds/job_seconds/stop_seconds each 1..30, artifacts exactly engine, kernel, init; errors "config template contract", "deadline contract", "artifact contract".

The envelope schema identity is derived from body.schema: metaviewer.role_switch(_result)/v0.3 -> role_switch_envelope/v0.3; rewind_request/event/v0.2 -> rewind_envelope/v0.2; headless_* and guest_command_* request/event v0.2 -> capsule_envelope/v0.2; anything else -> envelope/v0.2. Serve and Connect refuse an envelope whose declared schema does not equal this mapping.

Connect is the client-side transport used in production client mode (daemon run.go: ipc.Connect or connectStreaming dial cfg.SocketPath, $XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/metaviewer/core.sock). It refuses "complete client registration required" (registration must be from core to daemon with a session_id), "unix peer required", and "core peer credentials refused" when the core's UID differs.

Every outbound reply is wrapped by policy.Wrap under a lock and re-validated with policy.ValidateEnvelope before writing (error prefix "outbound contract: "). The handler is first called with the registration under HelloTimeout, then the configured daemon hello (registration.Body) is sent.

Two lanes: ctrlCh (cap 64) for take_control, release_control and metaviewer.role_switch, and a data lane staged through a FIFO of up to 256 pending items feeding dataCh (cap 64). When the backlog reaches 256 the stager stops reading dataIn, which blocks the socket reader. Errors go through fail(), which keeps the first error and cancels the session.

On a clean core hang-up Framer.Read returns io.EOF; exitLoop drains the workers and returns that io.EOF as the error when no session error occurred, and run.go prints it and exits with status 2. Abnormal read, framing, validation, route, schema or auth failures cancel the session before the workers are joined.

Inbound refusals end the session: "registered core route refused" (schema mismatch, from/to/session_id differ from the registration, seq 0 or empty nonce), "authenticated core hello required before requests" (capsule/rewind envelope before core hello/v0.2), "core surface request required" (body schema not hello, capsule_state_request, surface_request, metaviewer.role_switch, headless_request, guest_command_request or rewind_request), plus any ValidateEnvelope, Authenticate or Reserve error.

Each control item creates a done channel that becomes ctrlGate; data queued after it waits for that control operation to finish, so data never overtakes a take_control or release_control, while control is never head-of-line blocked behind data.

Config is the transport policy shared by Listen, Serve, Connect, NewFramer and NewPolicy: socket path, admitted UID, JSON bounds, replay/connection caps and the hello/read/write/probe/shutdown timeouts. Production builds it in internal/daemon/environment.go with MaxFrameBytes 1<<20, MaxDepth 32, MaxStringBytes 65536, MaxKeys 256, MaxArrayItems 4096, MaxConnections 1 and socket $XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/metaviewer/core.sock.

Frozen ceilings: MaxFrameBytes <= 1048576, MaxDepth <= 32, MaxStringBytes <= 65536, MaxKeys <= 256, MaxArrayItems <= 4096, otherwise error "frozen transport ceiling exceeded". Every limit must be explicit (>= 1, MaxFrameBytes >= 2), SocketPath non-empty, HelloTimeout in (0, 5s], ReadTimeout in (0, 30s], Write/Probe/Shutdown timeouts > 0, otherwise "explicit transport policy required"; the adapter then refuses to start.

Framer reads and writes newline-delimited JSON frames over one Unix connection, with separate read and write mutexes. The bufio reader is sized min(MaxFrameBytes, 4096); NewFramer refuses an invalid Config or a nil connection ("connection required").

arm sets the socket deadline to the earlier of now+timeout and the context deadline, and registers context.AfterFunc to force the deadline to now on cancellation, so a blocked read or write unblocks when the session context is cancelled.

A frame including its trailing newline may not exceed MaxFrameBytes ("frame limit exceeded"); EOF after a partial line returns io.ErrUnexpectedEOF; each frame must then pass ValidateJSON. Every read is bounded by ReadTimeout or a sooner context deadline.

Outbound frames of MaxFrameBytes or more, or containing CR or LF, are refused with "invalid outbound frame"; outbound JSON is re-validated with ValidateJSON; a zero-byte write returns io.ErrShortWrite. Writes are bounded by WriteTimeout.

A \u escape in the DC00-DFFF range, or a D800-DBFF escape not followed by a valid low-surrogate escape, marks the frame as invalid (ValidateJSON returns "lone surrogate escape"). Duplicate object keys are refused rather than silently overwritten.

ValidateJSON is the token-level bound applied to every frame before schema decoding. Refusal strings: "invalid JSON encoding" (empty or non-UTF-8), "string limit" (> MaxStringBytes), "depth limit" (>= MaxDepth), "key limit" (> MaxKeys), "invalid or duplicate key", "array limit" (> MaxArrayItems), "unclosed container", "extra JSON value", "lone surrogate escape".

An admitted envelope whose msg_id starts with "core-keepalive-" and whose body is surface_request/v0.2 op "list" is the core liveness probe. It is answered with the fixed body surface_event/v0.2 event "error" code "DAEMON_KEEPALIVE" detail "core-keepalive" without calling the handler, so it never enumerates surfaces or changes capsule state.

Envelope carries schema, msg_id, ts_ns, from/to endpoints, session_id, seq, nonce and a raw body. Policy is supplied by the authority integration: ValidateEnvelope must validate the closed body before Reserve runs, Authenticate binds the sender instance and pinned hello, Reserve records (session, component, instance) seq+nonce and must survive reconnect and restart, Wrap allocates the adapter's own sequence and identity.
Peer credentials come from SO_PEERCRED on the Unix socket. Admission compares only the UID against Config.UID; PID and GID are read but not checked here.

The schema pattern ^/dev/shm(/[A-Za-z0-9_][A-Za-z0-9._-]{0,127}){1,8}$ is replaced by a hand-written check: 10-255 bytes, prefix /dev/shm/, 1 to 8 segments each matching ^[A-Za-z0-9_][A-Za-z0-9._-]{0,127}$.

NewPolicy compiles the v0.2 JSON schema files from a supplied fs.FS into a closed validator plus the caller-supplied Authority (Authenticate, Reserve, Wrap). It refuses "schema filesystem and authority required", and any panic while compiling becomes "malformed contract schema: ..." so a bad deployment schema never admits partially.

Only a closed schema subset is supported. Compile refusals: "nonlocal schema reference", "unsupported reference fragment", "invalid schema pointer", "missing schema reference", "cyclic schema", "invalid ref", "unsupported type union", "unsupported type", "open schema refused" (additionalProperties not false, or object without closure), "empty oneOf refused", "invalid pattern", "unsupported schema keyword <k>".

envelope.schema.json must be a closed object with schema const envelope/v0.2 and a oneOf body ("closed v0.2 envelope contract required"). Optional files must also be closed if present: capsule_envelope.schema.json with exactly 4 body choices, rewind_envelope.schema.json with exactly 2, guest_command_observation_envelope.schema.json with body ref schema guest_command_observation/v0.2; otherwise "closed capsule envelope contract required", "closed rewind envelope contract required", "closed command observation contract required".

ValidateEnvelope refusals: "unconfigured schema policy", "frame limit" (len > MaxFrameBytes), ValidateJSON errors, "closed envelope object required", "unknown envelope discriminator" (schema not envelope/v0.2, capsule_envelope/v0.2, rewind_envelope/v0.2, guest_command_observation_envelope/v0.2 or role_switch_envelope/v0.3), "role switch route refused", and "closed v0.2 envelope/body refused" (schema mismatch, absent optional contract, or terminal length check).

For body schema terminal_session/v0.2 with op data or write, params.b64 and an integer params.byte_count are required and byte_count must equal the base64 decoded length (len/4*3 minus padding); otherwise the envelope is refused.

Validation rules: oneOf must match exactly one branch; closed objects refuse unknown keys; string length limits count runes; integers must be plain lexemes (^-?(0|[1-9][0-9]*)$) within +/-9007199254740991; minimum and maximum are compared exactly with big.Rat; maxProperties is enforced on objects.

role_switch_envelope/v0.3 reuses the envelope/v0.2 header and closes the body to three shapes: metaviewer.role_switch/v0.3 request, or metaviewer.role_switch_result/v0.3 with ok true, or with ok false plus code matching ^[A-Z][A-Z0-9_]*$ (1-64 chars). request_id and surface_id are 1-128 chars matching ^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._:-]{0,127}$; role is "human" or "agent".
A role switch request is accepted only from component core to daemon, and a role switch result only from daemon to core; any other direction makes ValidateEnvelope return "role switch route refused".

Serve is the server-side adapter loop (daemon run.go uses it when the runtime is not in client mode). It requires listener, policy, handler and log ("listener, complete policy, handler and log required"); every refusal writes the single line "adapter: connection refused" to the log and closes the connection, with no reason sent to the peer.
Connections beyond cfg.MaxConnections are refused at accept time (log line "adapter: connection refused", socket closed); production sets MaxConnections to 1.

Per connection: SO_PEERCRED UID check, then the first frame must arrive within HelloTimeout and carry body schema hello/v0.2; every envelope must match EnvelopeSchema(body), have seq != 0, a non-empty nonce, from core and to daemon. Order is ValidateEnvelope -> Authenticate -> Reserve -> handler; any failure ends the connection. Later reads are bounded by ReadTimeout (idle).

Replies are wrapped by policy.Wrap and written synchronously, so backpressure is kept without an unbounded send queue; a write error ends the connection silently, and ctx.Err() is checked before every Wrap and write so nothing is sent after cancellation.

On shutdown Serve cancels the context, closes the listener and all client sockets, and waits up to ShutdownTimeout for handler goroutines; if a handler ignores ctx it returns "handler shutdown deadline exceeded" instead of hanging.

RuntimeSocketPath requires an absolute runtime directory ("absolute runtime directory required") that is a 0700 directory owned by the UID ("unsafe runtime directory") and is not a symlink ("symlink runtime directory"); it creates <dir>/metaviewer with 0700 and returns <dir>/metaviewer/surfaces.sock.

Listen refuses: "absolute socket path required", unsafe or symlinked parent ("unsafe runtime directory", "symlink socket parent"), an existing path that is not a 0600 socket of the UID ("unsafe existing socket"), a live listener ("socket already served"), a dial error other than ECONNREFUSED ("socket staleness unproven"), an inode swapped during the probe ("socket changed during probe"), and a bound socket not 0600/owned ("unsafe bound socket"). Only a proven-stale socket is removed. Bind uses umask 0177.

Listen changes the process-wide umask to 0177 around bind; the comment requires calling it before other filesystem writers start, because a concurrent file creation would inherit the restrictive umask.
CloseListener removes the socket path only if it is still the same inode bound by this listener; a replaced socket is left alone and reported as "socket replaced before cleanup".
maxWireMonoNS is (1<<53)-1; it is the ceiling for capture_mono_ns, session-relative mono_ns and the Handle clock check (record.go base()).

capture runs <BinDir>/<family> frame --container <c> [--window <w>] after capsule.RefuseProtectedContainer, parses one JSON line (1<<20 bound) and checks seq, width, height and capture_mono_ns. Errors: "invalid frame metadata", "unexpected Holdings window", "invalid frame window binding", "invalid frame generation", "stale or over-rate frame" (generation not increasing, or interval < 1e9/fps ns).

Before copying, geometry must fit (width*height*4 <= MemoryBytes, "frame geometry exceeds memory"), the path must be under the surface FramesRoot ("frame is outside surface RAM root"), the file must fit the ring ("frame exceeds ring"), the PNG size must match ("PNG geometry mismatch"), every pixel must be opaque ("RGB frame must be opaque"), and SHA-256 of the RGB24 pixels must equal sha256_rgb24 ("RGB witness mismatch").

Verified PNG bytes are copied into a private /dev/shm/metaviewer-record-* directory. When the ring is full the oldest copies are deleted and a "dropped" event with policy "ram_ring_oldest" and dropped_frames is emitted before "frame_captured" (ram_path, sha256, byte_count). An unlink failure mid-eviction keeps the remaining frames and deletes the new copy.
Refusal details shown to the core are sanitized: path and syscall wrappers are unwrapped, and any message that still contains "/" is replaced by a fixed fallback, so host paths do not reach the UI.

Directory export writes <recording_id>-<sha256>.tar with O_CREAT|O_EXCL|O_NOFOLLOW mode 0600, frames named frame-%06d.png. Refusal details (reason_code POLICY): "DESTINATION_UNAVAILABLE: export destination path exceeds contract bound", "...export exceeds contract byte bound" (> 1<<30), "...destination grant was replaced" (pinned dev/inode changed), "DESTINATION_EXISTS: recording destination already exists". A partial file is unlinked only if it is still the same inode.

Exact .tar file export has the same O_EXCL no-overwrite rule and the same DESTINATION_UNAVAILABLE / DESTINATION_EXISTS refusals, plus "DESTINATION_UNAVAILABLE: invalid file path". The file is fsynced and checked against the path inode before the "exported" event (destination_capability_id, destination_path, sha256, byte_count).

Package record owns bounded RAM captures and explicitly authorized exports: callers register admitted surfaces, send record_request/v0.2 through Manager.Handle and drive Manager.Poll from their scheduler. There is no background process; disk export is a sealed tar of PNG frames; Release is local only (no wire operation).

NewManager refuses "invalid recorder configuration" (RingBytes 0, > 1<<30 or > MemoryBytes, MaxFPS 0 or > 120), "CLI binary directory required", "invalid destination" and "invalid surface binding" (family must be srf-identity-surface or srf-holdings-capsule, identity window ^w[0-9]+$, FramesRoot under /dev/shm). A destination directory, or the parent of a .tar destination, is pinned by dev/inode at construction.

Production recorder: MemoryBytes 64<<20, RingBytes 8<<20, MaxFPS 30, CLI runner from MV_SRF_BIN_DIR with 1<<20 output limit and 90s timeout. Disk export is enabled only when MV_RECORDING_DESTINATION is set; MV_RECORDING_CAPABILITY_ID defaults to "recording:configured".

Unregistering a surface seals its active recordings as abortedByDestroy, removes their owned frame copies (keeping any that fail to delete and their bytes), drops the ring reservation only when all copies are gone, and runs unregister hooks. An aborted capture can no longer be exported by disk_start.

Disk export needs the exact configured grant: no destination gives POLICY "DESTINATION_UNSET: recording destination is not configured"; a capability id or path that differs from the configured one gives POLICY "DESTINATION_UNSET: host destination is not authorized". refuse() builds the refused event and a *Refusal error with the same code.

record_request/v0.2 parameters are closed per op: ram_start = surface_id, recording_id, ring_bytes, max_fps; disk_start = surface_id, recording_id, destination_capability_id, destination_path, max_fps; ram_stop/disk_stop = surface_id, recording_id; screenshot = surface_id, capture_id. Errors: "invalid record request", "unknown record operation", "closed record parameters required", "missing record parameter" (absent or null). These are Go errors with no refused event.

Handle returns a record_event/v0.2 event "refused" with reason_code and detail: POLICY "monotonic clock exceeded wire ceiling", POLICY "surface is not admitted", POLICY "invalid recording bounds" (ring 0 or > 1<<30, fps 0 or > 120), BUDGET_EXCEEDED "recording exceeds configured limits", BUDGET_EXCEEDED "session memory exceeded" (sum of ring reservations > MemoryBytes), POLICY "recording identity was already used" (also for released IDs).

A disk_start on a sealed ram or screenshot capture of the same surface (not released, not aborted by destroy) exports the existing capture instead of starting a new one. Screenshot mode captures once with fps 1 and is sealed immediately (started, frame events, stopped). ram and disk modes register an active recording that Poll advances.
Poll refuses "recorder is closed", "request identity required", and Refusal POLICY "recording is not active" for unknown or sealed recordings; otherwise it runs one capture.

Stopping refuses POLICY "recording is not active in this mode and surface" (unknown, sealed, other surface, or disk_stop vs ram mode mismatch). For disk mode the export runs before sealing; an export failure returns a refused event (POLICY with DESTINATION_* detail) and leaves the recording active so the stop can be retried.

Release only works on sealed captures (ErrUnknownRecording "unknown recording", ErrActiveRecording "recording is active"); it deletes owned RAM copies only, frees the ring reservation and keeps a tombstone so the ID can never be reused. A failed remove keeps the reservation for retry.

Close removes only the private RAM workspace (metaviewer-record-* under /dev/shm), closes the destination pin, seals every recording and runs close hooks; producer-owned frames are never deleted. After Close every call returns "recorder is closed".

Frames are opened only under /dev/shm/ through O_NOFOLLOW directory traversal and must be regular files on tmpfs (statfs magic 0x01021994); errors "frame is outside RAM", "frame is not a regular file", "frame is not on tmpfs".

Protected inputs must be canonical (no symlink alias, "canonical absolute path", "path alias"), regular, single-link, owned by root or the user, not group/other writable (and 0600 user-owned when private), within the size limit, and unchanged across the read ("protected regular file required", "file changed").

inventory-config.json (<= 65536 bytes, private 0600) must be schema arm64-resource-inventory-config/v1 with hex run_id 24, source_commit 40, hashes 64 and actor = "actor-"+sha256("agent:agent-arm64-"+run_id) ("configuration identity"); root under /dev/shm/ named metaviewer-arm64-<run_id>-* with journal allocations.jsonl ("configuration root"); exactly 3 producer pins ("producer pin set", "producer missing", "producer source binding"); image pins ("image set", "image pin"); browser images require the mv_identity.py provisioner pin.

Before and after each transaction the root directory and allocations.jsonl/allocations.lock must still be the opened inodes with private modes; otherwise "inventory root replaced" or "inventory file replaced".

The inventory is active only when MV_ARM64_CAPSULES=1 (otherwise OpenFromEnv returns nil, nil and nothing is recorded). It needs MV_ARM64_INVENTORY_CONFIG ("protected configuration required"), producer name graphical or guestcommand ("producer identity"), a verified descriptor, and the running executable path equal to the pinned producer path ("producer executable path").

Opening a producer refuses "private root required" (root not 0700 user-owned), "private ledger file", "setup admission absent" (no header, guardian or bound app, or already sealed) and "producer already attempted": producer-<name>.lock is created with O_EXCL, so a producer can open the ledger only once per run and is never resumed.

The producer must run inside the guardian cgroup recorded in the ledger ("producer outside guardian", "guardian inode"), with memory.high 6442450944, memory.max 8589934592, memory.swap.max 0 ("guardian memory limits") and cpu.max quota non-zero and <= 2x period ("guardian CPU limits").
