Package resourceinventory records allocations in a hash-chained JSONL journal before effects happen; it never infers absence from missing evidence and never resumes a crashed producer. Limits: maxJournal 8<<20 bytes, maxRows 8192, maxPayload 65536 bytes, integers <= 9007199254740991.

Each payload stage has a closed field list (stageFields). Refusals: "unknown stage", "closed payload fields", "missing <k>", "producer" (not setup/graphical/guestcommand), "stage owner" (native_* only graphical, service_* only guestcommand, others setup), "numeric payload", "string payload" (empty or > 4096), hex length checks (source_commit 40, hashes and cid 64, invocation 32), "native PID identity", "image identity" (sha256:<64 hex>).

Every read re-verifies the whole journal: it must end in a newline and be <= 8 MiB ("torn or oversized journal"), have <= 8192 rows ("row bound"), each row capsule_resource_inventory/v0.2 with seq = index+1, prev = previous sha256 (64 zeros first) and sha256 = SHA-256(seq\nprev\npayload) ("chain mismatch"); no row after a seal ("write after seal"); first row must be the session header ("header required"). Errors are prefixed "resource inventory: ".

Stage order: session header (must equal Config.header, "header binding"), guardian_bound ("guardian binding"), app_pending and app_bound ("app admission", "app binding"), then *_pending -> *_bound -> *_closed/helper_removed per resource ("allocation admission", "foreign native allocation", "foreign identity helper", "foreign identity helper tuple", "foreign helper allocation", "service name", "unreserved allocation", "duplicate binding", "native binding", "service binding", "closure without binding"), unknown rows, producer_sealed ("producer seal sequence") and coordinator_sealed ("coordinator seal").

Append refusals before any write: "producer fenced" (closed or poisoned), "foreign producer", root/file replacement, "shared inventory lock busy", "producer already sealed", "setup header absent", "payload bound" (> 65536). The new row is appended to a candidate copy and the whole journal is re-parsed first, so a journal that would exceed 8 MiB or 8192 rows refuses the append with "torn or oversized journal" or "row bound" and writes nothing.

Once bytes may have reached the journal, any failure poisons the producer: a short or failed write returns "append uncertain", and a failed fsync of journal or root, or a replaced root after writing, also sets poisoned. Every later Append then returns "producer fenced" and nothing more is written.

Append refuses caller keys that collide with stage, producer or id ("reserved payload key"). Seal writes producer_sealed with last_seq = this producer's last row, then closes the producer and all files even if the seal write failed; Unknown writes stage unknown with reason "allocation outcome uncertain".
All producers share allocations.lock: an exclusive non-blocking flock is retried every 5 ms for up to 2 seconds, then "resource inventory: shared inventory lock busy".

Native evidence comes from /usr/bin/docker --host unix:///var/run/docker.sock with PATH=/usr/bin:/bin, a 5 second timeout and 1<<20 bytes of output ("Docker metadata bound"); any failure is "Docker metadata unavailable".

Before a native capsule starts, Pending records native_pending. It refuses "unconfigured native allocation" (profile not allowed for kind, container name not srf-vm-/srf-id-/srf-pg-<profile>, or no image) and "payload inode custody" (payload directory not uid/gid 10001 mode 0700).

Binding re-observes the native capsule twice and fails with "unreserved native binding", "returned native tuple", "native state corroboration", "native Docker identity or limits" (memory 0 or > 8<<30, swap != memory), "VM memory limits" (VM must be exactly 8<<30), "native payload mount", "native payload absent", "payload changed", "native process unobserved", "native container changed", "native process changed", "native state changed". Bound writes an unknown row on any failure.

Closure requires proof of absence: container CID gone, recorded PID absent or with a different start time, and native-state file removed. Otherwise it writes an unknown row and returns "native closure lacks bound identity", "native CID closure unknown", "native PID closure unknown" or "native state closure unknown".

ProcessRunner runs the operator view helper srf-identity-surface from MV_SRF_BIN_DIR; Run allows only view-stop and paste-text (else code "usage" "unsupported operator command") after RefuseProtectedContainer.

Start allows only `srf-identity-surface view|login --container <srf-(id|pg|vm)-...>` (else "usage" "invalid view command") and refuses "configuration" "private operator state directory required" unless MV_SRF_STATE_DIR is an absolute clean 0700 directory reached without symlinks, and "operator state owner mismatch" for a foreign owner.

The helper runs in its own process group; cancel sends SIGINT to the group with a 15 s WaitDelay so it can restore read-only mode, then the group is SIGKILLed on reap. killGroup refuses "refused" "unsafe view process identity" for pid <= 1, the adapter pid or its group.

Start waits up to 30 s for the first stdout line: launch error gives "execution" "view launch failed"; early exit gives an exit fault for srf-identity-surface or "malformed_cli" "view exited before announcement"; timeout gives "unavailable" "view readiness deadline"; the line is then validated by parseInfo.
Only the first newline-terminated stdout line (max 65536 bytes) is kept as the announcement; an oversized line sends nil, which fails parsing; later output is discarded.
view.Manager tracks operator views (view or login) per identity capsule, one foreground helper per capsule, without granting agent admission; New() with no runner refuses every call.

Every operation first refuses protected containers, then "usage" "invalid identity capsule" for ids not matching ^srf-(id|pg|vm)-[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]{0,39}$, and "configuration" "operator view runner required" with no runner.
Open refuses "refused" "view unavailable or already registered" when closed, already open or busy, and "refused" "manager closed" if closed during start; the view is forgotten when the helper exits.
Stop/Paste refuse "surface" "unknown view" for no registered view and "refused" "view operation pending" while another operation runs.
Stop always closes the helper, then requires a view-stop receipt with stopped_view == id, pid > 1 and 0 <= seconds <= 60, else "malformed_cli" "invalid view stop receipt".

Paste accepts 1..16384 bytes of valid UTF-8 (else "usage" "paste requires bounded UTF-8 text"), only on a login view ("refused" "login view required"), and requires pasted_runes equal to the rune count ("malformed_cli" "invalid paste receipt").

A view announcement must be http://127.0.0.1:<1..65535> with no user info or fragment, a non-empty native field and an absolute socket path; else "malformed_cli" "invalid view announcement" or "invalid loopback view port".

SCOPE.md states the rewind package is an opt-in ARM64 backend candidate not registered with core, Go, the UI or the default daemon by itself; it reuses guest_command_runtime for protocol, validation, image builder and native helpers.

Documented point rules: at most two published immutable full-RAM points; a new mark stages a temporary third snapshot under the same RAM ceiling, verifies hashes, publishes, and evicts only the oldest unmapped point; failed staging preserves both prior points; failed restore keeps the point and enters uncertainty.

Documented custody: dedicated child-free cgroup under newton-ia.slice with MemoryHigh at most 6 GiB, MemoryMax at most 8 GiB, swap 0, CPU at most 2 cores, TasksMax at most 256; 32-GiB global headroom gate; VM stays 256 MiB and one vCPU; no whole-VM TTL for this profile [CITED: daemon-adapter/rewind_runtime/SCOPE.md].

Rewind host config rewind-host-config/v1: explicit runtime_admitted, owner_id, runtime_root under /dev/shm/ ('RAM root required'), startup_seconds/stop_seconds 1..10, and the four artifact sha256 values must equal APPROVED ('reviewed artifact set required').

rewind_runtime Controller serializes one Native ARM64 VMM owner: phases new, initializing, ready, pausing, paused, marking, resuming, restoring, running, uncertain, stopping, stopped. status reports cancel_supported false.

Only one operation runs at a time: a non-blocking lock raises 'actor busy'; after stop is requested every entry raises 'owner stopping'. Request IDs are single-use with a cap of 1024 ('request replay/capacity').

pause needs ready ('already paused'); mark and resume need paused ('pause required'); restore is also allowed from uncertain when recoverable. resume/restore need a next binding with the same workload and strictly greater generation and authority_epoch and a new session and reservation ('stale host authority', 'reused session'). A failed mark rolls back the point map; a failed restore closes the VMM and sets recoverable only if the stream and process are gone and the ledger is not poisoned.

Rewind run reuses prepare_exec, needs phase ready ('command not admitted'), unique job_id (1024 cap), a deadline of timeout_ms+5 s, ordered output at most 65536 bytes total ('output bound'), job_empty true and exact byte accounting ('output byte accounting'). Any failure moves the owner to uncertain.
stop is an independent close path usable during a blocked run: it sets the stop fence, calls native.stop, and reports stopped only if proof closed is true; any failure leaves phase uncertain.

The rewind cgroup must be under newton-ia.slice with memory.high at most 6 GiB, memory.max at most 8 GiB, pids.max at most 256, swap 0, cpu.max at most 2 CPUs, no nested cgroups and exact membership; messages 'dedicated rewind slice', 'unbounded resource', 'swap forbidden', 'CPU bound', 'nested cgroup unproved', 'foreign cgroup member'.
The rewind ledger is append-only, hash-chained, fsynced and bounded to 4 MiB ('ledger bound'); any write error sets poisoned ('ledger poisoned').

A base-directory .rewind-owner.lock flock excludes another owner, and any other entry in the base refuses with 'prior runtime requires reconciliation'; the fix is explicit sealed recovery (tools/rewind_recover.py), never takeover.

Allocation native checks: 'allocation cannot replay', 'runtime not admitted', 'ARM64 Linux required', cgroup scope, 'global headroom' (32 GiB), 'private process umask required' (0077), KVM checks, 'RAM filesystem required' (/dev/shm device), base lock, pinned assets; then writes fc/Image/initrd.gz, seals recovery.json, spawns Firecracker, boots 256 MiB/1 vCPU with mv_rewind=1, and waits for a quiescent fence.

Mark requires paused with no stream and an unused point_id ('point admission'), picks the oldest unmapped victim when two points exist ('all points mapped'), requires 300 MiB free ('snapshot headroom') and total staged ring bytes within 1 GiB ('staged ring byte admission', 'ring byte ceiling'), takes a Full snapshot, pins state and mem files, and publishes the new pair while retiring the victim.

After boot, resume or restore, the guest is reseeded over vsock with an RWR1 length-prefixed rewind_guest_reset/v0.2 request (max 4096 bytes, 3 s); the reply must echo session/epoch/generation/challenge, report commands_fenced true and a fresh 64-hex guest_nonce, then an MVGC hello/ready must match the binding. This prevents a restored RAM image from reusing old authority.

Stop always attempts close_process even if the ledger is poisoned, but then raises 'closed process but journal ownership unresolved'. Removal requires the same runtime directory identity and only expected files ('untracked runtime files retained').

The ledger history must be a closed shape: owner intent/complete pairs, run intent/complete with output at most 65536 bytes, mark intent then published, restore only of published points; anything else is 'unknown or uncertain ledger operation', and any open operation is 'operation incomplete'.
recover_owned purges exactly one sealed dead rewind allocation under /dev/shm after durable proof: it never starts, signals or scans workloads. Called only by tools/rewind_recover.py.

Recovery requires: base and root identities equal the caller's retained expected custody ('base replaced', 'root replaced'), only the lock and one root in the base ('foreign base member'), a matching recovery seal ('seal mismatch'), the original cgroup absent not just empty ('original cgroup not absent'), ledger sha256 equal to expected ('unexpected ledger'), a sealed allocation origin ('unsealed allocation'), no spawn in flight ('spawn in flight or identity absent'), and every recorded PID absent from /proc ('PID present or reused').

Before deleting, assets and published points must still match, only known members may exist ('unknown runtime member'), a proof file is written exclusively outside the base ('proof must survive purge'), and everything is re-checked ('resource appeared', 'inventory changed', 'member changed').
The runner requires its cgroup memory.max exactly 536870912, memory.swap.max 0, pids.max exactly 64 and a cpu quota no larger than its period ('service resource caps', 'service cpu cap').

Service entrypoint launched by the Go owner as python -I -B runner.py <attempt>. It checks attempt custody, an exact launch.json field set, re-pins each bundle file, requires exactly the 11 guest_command_runtime modules ('closed package required'), checks it runs in its own unit cgroup ('dedicated service required') and the caps, execs modules from verified bytes, prints the ready line and runs the Controller.

Modules are compiled from verified bytes and inserted into sys.modules (no import from disk), and the Go side passes -B, so the service itself writes no __pycache__. Inferred: a __pycache__ appearing in a source package comes from other runs, not this runner.

Headless service entrypoint: same custody checks with launch fields files/config/state_dir/runtime_root/unit, loads mc06-controller arm_backend, contract_guard and controller from verified bytes, prints {"mc09_ready":true,...}, then handles one JSON line at a time bounded by the controller MAX_RECORD.

rewind_recover.py inserts the daemon-adapter directory on sys.path and imports rewind_runtime and guest_command_runtime normally. Inferred: run without -B or PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE it can create __pycache__ inside those source packages.

CLI for sealed ARM64 rewind orphan recovery: --config, --root, --expected (retained trusted custody JSON with base, root, ledger_sha256), --proof (new file outside the base). Any OSError/RuntimeError/ValueError prints 'recovery refused: <message>' to stderr and exits 1; success prints schema rewind-recovery-result/v1 with proof_sha256.

The rewind service loads exactly 8 guest_command_runtime modules (NORMAL) and 4 rewind_runtime modules (REWIND) from verified bundle bytes; any other entry is 'closed source set' and a missing one 'missing source'.

Adapter maps private packets to the backend: guest cancel is always refused UNAVAILABLE; create failure emits outcome_unknown TRANSPORT; a ready-state mark is composed as pause, mark with deferred publication, and resume with the new binding; rewind failures emit rewind_event outcome_unknown with code NATIVE, followed by recovery_ready (no_active_vmm true) when a failed restore is recoverable.

Stop emits accepted, then always calls backend.stop even if persisting failed; it waits 5 s for any running job ('actor close unproved'). Success emits stopped native_absent true; any failure emits outcome_unknown code CLEANUP with phase uncertain and ownership held.

Non-stop packets go into a queue of 4 (put_nowait; overflow ends input), a second stop is 'duplicate stop dispatch', and stop runs on its own thread. While idle in ready or paused, a failed native.live() check emits outcome_unknown code PROCESS_IDENTITY on the create request. Any input failure ends in RuntimeError('private input failure').

Offline package build entry: requires MV_PKG_OUT and CAPSULE_UI_KIT_REPO (set -u ':?' aborts otherwise), runs node --test ui/test/nesting.test.js, then execs ui/tools/package.js. Node binary is MV_NODE_BIN or node.

Needs MV_PKG_OUT, CAPSULE_UI_KIT_REPO and one of MV_ELECTRON_ZIP_DIR or ELECTRON_OVERRIDE_DIST_PATH; without the Electron source it prints 'Set MV_ELECTRON_ZIP_DIR or ELECTRON_OVERRIDE_DIST_PATH to local Electron files' and exits 1. No network fetch is done.

Refusals: 'BLOCKED: tests/e2e/run.py absent', 'E2E_PREREQ: pinned kit checkout absent' (CAPSULE_UI_KIT_REPO or MV_KIT_CHECKOUT), 'Node >=24 required', 'Electron pin mismatch' (must be 44.9.2), 'local Electron archive required', 'Electron archive checksum mismatch', 'unsafe Electron archive path', 'incomplete Electron dist; repair explicitly', 'Electron binary version mismatch'. npm ci only with --offline.

The volume-e2e job in .github/workflows/volume.yml must contain (in non-comment lines) '[ ! -f "$HARNESS" ]', 'setup-node@', 'kit-checkout', 'npm ci' and 'install_electron.cjs', else 'E2E_PREREQ: volume workflow missing ...'.

Offline volume e2e driver: prepare the staged kit, then run tests/e2e/run.py --iterations 20 or 300 times printing 'volume-e2e i/N PASS'; --prepare-only, --check-workflow. Exit 2 for BLOCKED: errors, 1 for others.

Provisions the asset directory from a local release directory or an HTTPS base URL: copies SHA256SUMS and the tier's assets (T1: metaviewer and node tarballs; --capsules adds opensuperficies, images, vision-engine, wender-agent) into a temp dir, verifies each digest, then moves them in. Prints JUDGE_FETCH_OK arch= tier=.

Errors print 'JUDGE_ASSET: <reason> -- fix: ...' rc 2: non-https URL, HTTPS without a 64-hex --sums-sha256, 'SHA256SUMS digest mismatch', 'invalid or duplicate SHA256SUMS entry', 'SHA256SUMS has no entry for <name>', '<name> digest mismatch', redirect outside HTTPS, unsupported machine. Bad arguments give JUDGE_USAGE rc 2.

Judge entry point with subcommands doctor | install | run | stop and flags --before-install, --capsules, --yes, --no-firewall. T1 is the packaged app alone; --capsules selects T2 (app plus browser capsule images, network, profile directory). There is no start subcommand and no --arm64 flag in this launcher.
Every typed refusal prints 'JUDGE_<CODE>: <problem> -- fix: <command>' on stderr and exits 2; an unknown subcommand or flag prints JUDGE_USAGE and exits 64. Notes go to stderr as 'JUDGE_NOTE: ...'.

Argument parsing: first word is the subcommand, the rest must be --before-install, --yes, --capsules or --no-firewall; anything else -> usage (rc 64). HOME unset -> 'JUDGE_USAGE: HOME is not set' rc 64.

MV_JUDGE_HOME (default $XDG_DATA_HOME/metaviewer-judge or ~/.local/share/metaviewer-judge) is refused with JUDGE_USAGE if it contains whitespace, is /, the home itself, or is relative; JUDGE_HOME_PATH if a path component exceeds NAME_MAX or home+'run/smoke-processes/2147483647.pid' reaches PATH_MAX (fix: export MV_JUDGE_HOME="$HOME/mv-judge").

Environment knobs: MV_JUDGE_KIT, MV_JUDGE_ASSET_DIR (default <kit>/assets), MV_SRF_BIN_DIR, SRF_IDENTITY_STORE_ROOT, MV_JUDGE_PROFILE (default 'judge'), MV_JUDGE_SHM_DIR (/dev/shm), MV_JUDGE_APPARMOR_DIR, MV_JUDGE_FW_WITNESS (/run/srf-open-egress/rules.sha256), MV_JUDGE_FW_LIBEXEC, MV_JUDGE_FW_UNIT_DIR, MV_JUDGE_STOP_WAIT (30), MV_JUDGE_RUN_USER_ROOT, MV_JUDGE_PKG_TOOL, MV_JUDGE_RELEASE_BASE, MV_JUDGE_EUID. Arch maps x86_64->x64, aarch64->arm64. These are exported so preflight.sh sees the same values.

Every docker call is wrapped in timeout --kill-after=5: 120 s [CITED: scripts/judge/metaviewer-judge.sh] by default (MV_JUDGE_DOCKER_TIMEOUT), 1800 s [CITED: scripts/judge/metaviewer-judge.sh] for load/save/pull/build (MV_JUDGE_DOCKER_IMAGE_TIMEOUT).

Administrator commands only run through sudo_step, which prints the exact command and asks '[y/N]'; --yes is the only non-interactive consent. Returns 99 declined, 98 sudo missing; need_sudo_step turns those into JUDGE_SUDO ('required administrator step declined', 'sudo is not installed and you are not root', 'administrator step failed (rc N)').

install and run take an exclusive non-blocking flock on $MV_JUDGE_HOME/run/launcher.lock (fd 9). A second launcher gets 'JUDGE_RUNNING: another launcher owns run or install'; an unwritable home gives JUDGE_PIDFILE.
Archives are refused if any member is absolute, contains '..', does not match the expected top-level name, or (for app and deps) is anything other than a regular file or directory (no links).

Each asset's sha256 must equal its entry in <asset dir>/SHA256SUMS; on mismatch or missing entry the file is deleted if this run downloaded it and install stops with 'JUDGE_ASSET: <name> does not match the kit SHA256SUMS (expected ..., got ...)'.

Install never downloads SHA256SUMS: if it is absent, JUDGE_ASSET tells the judge to run fetch_assets.py --source <complete-release-directory>. Missing assets are downloaded from RELEASE_BASE (github releases v$VERSION) only after confirmation, with curl --proto =https --tlsv1.2, connect timeout MV_JUDGE_DOWNLOAD_CONNECT (60) and stall limit MV_JUDGE_DOWNLOAD_STALL (120). No curl -> JUDGE_SYSDEP; declined -> JUDGE_ASSET 'download declined'; failure -> JUDGE_ASSET 'download of <n> failed, stalled or was interrupted'.

Missing apt packages (from preflight --sysdep-packages) are installed via one confirmed 'apt-get update && apt-get install -y'. Declined/no sudo/failure -> JUDGE_SUDO; still missing afterwards -> 'JUDGE_SYSDEP: packages still missing after apt-get'.

If no Node with major >= 24 is found (kit node in $MV_JUDGE_HOME/node first, then PATH), node-linux-<arch>.tar.xz is verified and unpacked with unpack_node.py; a still-wrong version gives JUDGE_NODE 'major 24 is required'.

App install is staged: unpack to app.new, require executable MetaViewer-linux-<arch>/metaviewer, move old app to app.old, publish app.new as app, restore app.old if publish fails ('cannot publish extracted app; previous install preserved'), then delete app.old.

Only when kernel.apparmor_restrict_unprivileged_userns=1 and /etc/apparmor.d/metaviewer-judge differs from the kit profile: requires apparmor_parser (else JUDGE_USERNS 'sudo apt-get install -y apparmor') and runs one confirmed step 'install ... && apparmor_parser -r'.
package.js must import (needs @electron/asar). If not, npm ci --ignore-scripts runs in <kit>/ui; no npm -> JUDGE_NPM; npm ci failure or imports still failing -> JUDGE_SMOKE with the last 3 log lines.

Smoke ownership records under run/smoke-processes and run/smoke-roots must be owner-only (0700 dirs, 0600 files) and are never resolved by signalling a PID: a root is removed only when the leader and its whole session/group are gone. Live or unverifiable state prints JUDGE_SMOKE_ACTIVE or JUDGE_SMOKE_STATE and exits 2.

Install runs 'node package.js --verify-install <app dir>' (exact manifest check) then a 600 s [CITED: scripts/judge/metaviewer-judge.sh] '--smoke <tarball>' under a private /tmp/mvj.* TMPDIR. Failures: JUDGE_SMOKE 'package verification failed', 'the install smoke failed (rc N)', JUDGE_SMOKE_STATE 'cannot create private smoke state' / 'smoke ownership remains'. Success prints METAVIEWER_MAIN_SMOKE_OK. Log: $MV_JUDGE_HOME/logs/smoke.log.

T2 needs images opensuperficies-identity-browser-<arch>:0.1.1 (0.2.0 when open network is ready), opensuperficies-program-host-<arch>:0.1.0 and opensuperficies-desktop-<arch>:1.1.0; if any is missing images-linux-<arch>.tar is docker-loaded, failure -> JUDGE_IMAGE 'docker load of <asset> failed'.

T2 provisions identities and profile directories for MV_JUDGE_PROFILE plus mv-live-1..4 (and browser entries of MV_SRF_PROFILES) under SRF_IDENTITY_STORE_ROOT; each profile dir must end mode 0700 owned by uid 10001, set via a --network none docker run of the identity-browser image (no sudo). Errors are JUDGE_PROFILE ('not a valid profile pool', 'identity publication failed', 'cannot provision ... via Docker', 'not mode 0700 owned by uid 10001').

Open network needs the egress firewall: one confirmed root script that re-hashes apply.sh and the rules/service files, installs them and enables srf-open-egress.service. --no-firewall, missing files/tools, decline, no sudo, failure, or no witness afterwards all return 1 with a JUDGE_NOTE and install falls back to the legacy network (not a refusal).

Legacy network: requires srf-identity-surface and srf-egress-proxy executables, writes a private empty policy {schema browserid.proxy-policy/v1, approved {}} and runs the identity surface network setup. Failures are JUDGE_NET ('kit surface or proxy executable is absent', 'cannot provision private proxy metadata', 'supported proxy net up failed').

judge_receipt.json (schema metaviewer.judge_receipt/v1) records version, tier, arch, network_mode, node and docker versions, smoke marker, profile id, host facts and asset digests; no timestamp, pid or host path. run reads the tier back from it.

Install order: refuse if app running (JUDGE_RUNNING), reconcile smoke state (JUDGE_SMOKE_ACTIVE), preflight static, sysdeps, node, preflight display, extract app, AppArmor, verify+smoke; for T2 extract opensuperficies, vision-engine, wender-agent, load images, firewall or legacy note, profiles, net up; then preflight all, write receipt and print 'JUDGE_INSTALL_OK tier=.. network=.. receipt=..'. Open firewall active without the 0.2.0 image -> JUDGE_IMAGE.

run refuses JUDGE_NOT_INSTALLED if the app binary or receipt is missing or the receipt tier is not T1/T2, JUDGE_RUNNING if the pidfile names a live metaviewer process; for T2 in legacy mode it re-runs static preflight and 'net up', then preflight all must pass.

The app is started with 'env -i' and an allowlist (HOME, fixed PATH, USER, LANG, SHELL, XDG_RUNTIME_DIR, DISPLAY/XAUTHORITY/DBUS/WAYLAND, absolute TMPDIR and XDG_* dirs, recording destination, T2 MV_SRF_*/vision/wender vars) and '--ozone-platform=x11'. PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE is not in the list, so a user-exported value never reaches the app or its Python children; nothing under scripts/ sets it.

run stays in the foreground, writes the child pid to run/metaviewer.pid (failure kills the child and gives JUDGE_PIDFILE), forwards TERM/INT/HUP to the child, and returns the app's exit code; the pidfile is removed only if it still names that child.

srf-pg-* program containers are stopped only if named in a private (0600, owner) native receipt or audit.jsonl in the state dir/store; a name prefix alone never admits a program. srf-id-* containers are always stopped.

stop reads owned program receipts first, then sends SIGTERM to the recorded pid and waits MV_JUDGE_STOP_WAIT (30 s [CITED: scripts/judge/metaviewer-judge.sh]); timeout -> JUDGE_STOP_TIMEOUT with fix 'kill -KILL <pid>'.

stop is a census: leftover smoke state, srf-* containers (except srf-egress-proxy, which stays running), sockets, mv-pkg-*/mv-host-xpra-*/display roots, RAM entries and RAM admission records each print 'JUDGE_STOP_LEAK: ... -- fix: ...'; any leak ends with a count line and exit 2, otherwise JUDGE_STOP_CLEAN. Unset TMPDIR gives a JUDGE_NOTE that the private runtime census is incomplete.
doctor runs preflight --phase all (prints JUDGE_DOCTOR_OK tier=..) or, with --before-install, only --phase static (JUDGE_DOCTOR_OK ... phase=before-install). doctor changes nothing.

Read-only host checks called by metaviewer-judge.sh (doctor/install/run) with --tier T0|T1|T2 and --phase static|all|display; --facts prints key=value host facts, --sysdep-packages prints missing apt packages. Never calls sudo.
Refusals accumulate (FAILS); each prints 'JUDGE_<CODE>: <problem> -- fix: <command>'. Warnings and notes never change the exit code.
Non Ubuntu 24.04 hosts get 'JUDGE_OS: warning: ... the kit is only verified on Ubuntu 24.04' (not a refusal).
JUDGE_ARCH: unsupported machine unless uname -m is x86_64 or aarch64.
JUDGE_NODE: 'node is not installed' or 'major 24 or newer is required'; fix: run metaviewer-judge.sh install, which installs Node 24 from the kit after confirmation.

JUDGE_BUNDLE_ARCH: kit holds only the other architecture's metaviewer tarball, or installed ELF binaries (app, resources/bin/*, opensuperficies bin, vision/wender runtimes) have e_machine other than 62 (x64) or 183 (arm64).
JUDGE_SYSDEP lists missing packages for tools Xvfb, xdpyinfo, xauth, tar, zip, unzip, strace, git, sha256sum, python3, pip3 (plus docker for T2); fix 'sudo apt-get install -y <pkgs>'.
JUDGE_USERNS when kernel.apparmor_restrict_unprivileged_userns=1 and the metaviewer-judge AppArmor profile is not loaded; fix: install (loads the profile after confirmation; never --no-sandbox).
JUDGE_DISPLAY: Wayland-only session with empty DISPLAY (enable XWayland), DISPLAY not set (use xvfb-run -a for headless install or a desktop DISPLAY), xdpyinfo missing, or X server unreachable.
JUDGE_XDG_RUNTIME: /run/user/<uid> missing or not owned by you; fix: use a logind desktop session, or on WSL2 set systemd=true in /etc/wsl.conf and wsl --shutdown.

JUDGE_SHM: /dev/shm not tmpfs, or less free than 512 MiB (T1) / 1024 MiB (T2) [CITED: scripts/judge/preflight.sh]; fix 'sudo mount -o remount,size=4g /dev/shm'. Below 2560 MiB [CITED: scripts/judge/preflight.sh] on T2 only a warning note.

JUDGE_RAM: MemAvailable below floor (MemTotal/4 capped at 20 GiB) + 512 MiB [CITED: scripts/judge/preflight.sh]; below 6144 MiB [CITED: scripts/judge/preflight.sh] a note says UI capsule creation will be refused; unreadable meminfo is also JUDGE_RAM.
JUDGE_CPUSET only when MV_JUDGE_REQUIRE_CPUSET is set (default none): required CPUs not in cpuset.cpus.effective.

T2 Docker checks: JUDGE_DOCKER_HOST if DOCKER_HOST/DOCKER_CONTEXT set; JUDGE_DOCKER if 'docker info' fails or times out (fix: start docker, usermod -aG docker, or omit --capsules), engine is rootless, context inspect fails, or endpoint is not unix://; JUDGE_DOCKER_DESKTOP for Docker Desktop.
JUDGE_IMAGE 'image is not present' for any of the three capsule images; fix install --capsules.

JUDGE_NET: host routes (not br-*, docker*, srfo*) overlapping 172.30.80.0/24 or 172.29.0.0/16 [CITED: scripts/judge/preflight.sh]; in phase all with legacy network, srf-idnet must be internal 172.30.80.0/24 and srf-egress-proxy running.
JUDGE_PROFILE: invalid MV_SRF_PROFILES JSON, or a profile directory (MV_JUDGE_PROFILE and mv-live-2..4) not mode 0700 owned by uid 10001.
JUDGE_RAM_STALE refusal when 'python3 -I tools/mv_ram_admission.py reclaim --dry-run' reports would_remove; a missing tool or failed dry run is only a warning.
JUDGE_DISK: free space below 2 GB (T1) or 15 GB (T0/T2) [CITED: scripts/judge/preflight.sh] at home/install dir or Docker root; below 30 GB a warning note for T0/T2.

--facts prints arch, nproc, mem_total_kib, mem_available_kib, shm_avail_bytes, node_version and network=open|legacy; network is open only if the firewall witness is non-empty and srf-identity-surface capabilities lists net_modes including open.
JUDGE_ROOT: any tier except T0 refuses to run as uid 0 ('Electron cannot run safely as root (never --no-sandbox)') and exits 2 immediately.
Missing xpra, Xvfb, xauth or xdotool prints 'optional capability (JUDGE_HOST_PROGRAM): Host program disabled' and never gates browser or container programs.

Phase static: os arch bundle_arch xdg shm ram (+cpuset, docker, net for T2) and disk. Phase display: display only. Phase all: os arch node, then bundle_arch sysdep userns display xdg shm ram for non-T0, then T2 cpuset docker image net profile ram_stale, and disk. Any refusal -> 'JUDGE_PREFLIGHT_FAIL tier= phase= count=' rc 2, else 'JUDGE_PREFLIGHT_OK' rc 0.

Called by step_node to unpack the Node archive: one root, no absolute or '..' members, copies only regular files (mode 0755 or 0644) and replaces npm/npx links with small sh wrappers that exec bin/node on the npm cli js.
Any OSError/ValueError/TarError prints 'JUDGE_ASSET: <reason> -- fix: obtain a valid Node archive' rc 2; install then fails with JUDGE_ASSET 'cannot unpack node'.

AppArmor profile 'metaviewer' attached to /**/MetaViewer-linux-{x64,arm64}/metaviewer, unconfined except it grants userns so the Electron sandbox works on Ubuntu 24.04; install copies it to /etc/apparmor.d/metaviewer-judge. Remove with apparmor_parser -R and rm.
